1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Hardcore mode**: a per-world **permadeath** toggle on the new-world form, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v9 → v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver`), with **no worldgen change**
10	  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
11	  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again
12	  - **Architecture**: `hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved first in the engine so it overrides mode/difficulty. The two lethal damage seams divert to a new `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()` (sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator, leaves `isDead` cleared so the respawn screen never shows); `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore (the death transition sets the mode directly); the shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event. New `GameOverScreen` component + a `GameShell` delete-world path
13	- **Difficulty**: the game gains Minecraft's difficulty axis — **Peaceful**, **Easy**, **Normal**, and **Hard** — orthogonal to the game mode, picked at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v8 → v9** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
14	  - **Peaceful**: no hostile mobs spawn (and switching to Peaceful instantly despawns every hostile already around — a safe panic button, the boss included), health regenerates **twice as fast**, and an empty hunger bar never hurts you — full survival minus the danger, distinct from Creative
15	  - **Easy / Normal / Hard** scale two things together: **mob hit damage** (×0.5 / ×1 / ×1.5, applied at the strike — the per-mob templates are never mutated) and **hostile spawning** (cadence + the concurrent cap, ×16 → 8 / 16 / 24)
16	  - **Starvation** (new): an empty hunger bar now has a consequence — half a heart every few seconds, down to a difficulty-scaled floor. Easy stops at 5 hearts, Normal at half a heart, and **Hard can starve you to death**; Peaceful never starves. (This changes existing **Normal** worlds: previously a fully-empty hunger bar did nothing.)
17	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/difficulties.ts` holds the `Difficulty` union plus **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that each system reads, mirroring the game-mode predicate pattern. Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` + a v9 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV8toV9`); the spawn gate keys **only** on difficulty and the damage/threat gate **only** on game mode, so the two axes stay independent (Peaceful stops spawns even in Creative; Creative is invulnerable even on Hard). New `setDifficulty` command (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`); new `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`/`STARVATION_HP` tunables
18	- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
19	  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
20	  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact
21	  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide
22	  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them
23	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New `setGameMode`/`toggleFlight`/`creativeGiveItem` commands; new `FLY_SPEED`/`FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` tunables
24	
25	### Changed
26	
27	- **Pause menu reorganized into tabs**: the Esc menu had grown into one long scrolling column (action buttons, the game-mode grid, volume sliders, the skin picker, and a 12-row controls list). It's now split into **Game** (save / load / reset / quit + game mode), **Options** (sound + appearance), and **Controls** (the key reference), with **Back to Game** pinned on top. Pure presentation — no save-format, worldgen, or behavior change (`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`).
28	
29	## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21
30	
31	### Added
32	
33	- **XP & enchanting**: the game gains its first progression currency and a way to spend it, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural XP bar + effect-coloured table sprite, synthesized blip/shimmer). The save schema bumps **v6 → v7** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
34	  - **XP** (`state.xp`, banked points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level): earned from **mob kills** (hostiles more than passives, the **boss a jackpot**; babies give none, like drops — table in `mobXp.ts`), **mining ores** (scaled by rarity), and **fishing** catches. A green **XP bar** above the hotbar fills toward the next level with the level number over it. Unlike status effects, XP is a long-term currency and is **not cleared on death**
35	  - **Enchanting**: craft an **Enchanting Table** (2 diamond ore + 4 cobble) and right-click it to open the enchanting panel, then spend XP levels to enchant the **selected** tool/weapon/armor. Deterministic and player-chosen (no random rolls): four enchantments, each up to **level 3** — **Sharpness** (+melee damage), **Protection** (−incoming damage), **Efficiency** (+mining speed), and **Unbreaking** (probabilistically saves durability). Each maps to exactly one existing seam, the same one-reader-per-seam discipline as status effects
36	  - **Architecture**: enchantments are **per-item-instance data, like durability** (non-stackable gear, slot-cloned on insert), so the inventory algebra and persistence are reused — they ride the existing `SavedSlot` snapshot/restore (validated on load). XP/level math + the award/spend helpers live in `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts`; the readers + `canEnchant`/`applyEnchant` in `lib/game/enchantments.ts`. Enchanting is a new `enchant` command (not a recipe — `craft` produces a fixed result and can't mutate the held instance). The `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is appended (id 52) so existing saved block ids never shift; `xp` and per-slot `enchantments` are additive v7 fields, so pre-XP saves load clean
37	- **Status effects, brewing & potions**: the game gains its first timed-buff system — six effects, five of them brewed into potions at a new station, all on **zero new assets** (procedural flask/icon sprites + a synthesized "glug"). The save schema bumps **v5 → v6** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
38	  - **Effects** (`state.effects`, a Map of id → remaining seconds): **Speed** (×1.2 movement), **Strength** (+3 melee damage), **Regeneration** (heals on its own cadence, even at low hunger), **Fire Resistance** (lava can't burn you), **Water Breathing** (lungs stay full, no drowning), and **Poison** (chips you down but **never kills** — floors at half a heart). Each is read at exactly one existing seam (movement speed, attack damage, the lava/oxygen ticks, or a per-tick accumulator), so the simulation stays modular. Re-applying an effect refreshes to the longer remaining time; all are cleared on death
39	  - **Brewing Stand** (craft 3 cobble + 1 gold ore): a new interactive block — right-click to open its **Brewing** recipes, exactly like a furnace opens smelting, reusing the whole `station`-recipe pipeline. Glass bottles come first (3 glass → 3 bottles), then a bottle + one reagent brews a potion: **feather → Swiftness**, **gunpowder → Strength**, **wheat → Regeneration**, **coal → Fire Resistance**, **raw fish → Water Breathing** (all existing drops/crops, so no new worldgen). Drink with the **F** key (the eat key is potion-aware); drinking consumes the whole bottle
40	  - **Poison hazard**: eating **rotten flesh** has an 80% chance to poison you — a real downside to the most desperate food. Poison is the only effect with no potion
41	  - **HUD**: active effects show as a stacked top-left column of procedural icon + m:ss countdown, opposite the minimap, hidden when nothing is active. The projection is cached and rebuilt only when the rounded seconds change, so it re-renders ~1 Hz instead of every frame
42	  - **Architecture**: effects live in a new `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts` (helpers + `tickStatusEffects`, which runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks so the fire-resist/water-breathing gates are current). Poison uses a **new** `applyNonLethalDamage` rather than the killing `applyUnmitigatedDamage`. The `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift. Effects are additive on save v6 (a pure version bump; pre-effect saves load with none) and **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active
43	- **Dragon Lord tracker**: while the boss lives, its top-center health HUD now includes a rotating pointer toward it and its horizontal distance in blocks, making it possible to reacquire the fight after terrain or summoned mobs break line of sight. The values are rounded before entering the React snapshot to avoid sub-block render churn. This is transient UI state with **no save-format or worldgen impact**.
44	- **Fishing**: water was only ever a hazard to avoid — now it's a place to fish, a relaxed renewable food source with the odd lucky find, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural rod/fish sprite + synthesized splashes). **No save-format or worldgen change** — the cast is transient session state and the new items save by string id
45	  - **Fishing rod** (craft 3 wood + 2 string): right-click while aiming at water to **cast** a bobber. After a random wait it **dips with a splash** (a bite) — right-click again within ~1.2 s to **reel in** a catch; miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing
```

Mending closes that loop by turning XP, the game's\nlong-term currency, into a way to maintain your best gear.\n\nMending is a fifth enchantment applied at the existing table (like Unbreaking,\nit takes any durable tool/weapon/armor). It's binary (max level 1). While it's\non the item you're holding or wearing, XP you pick up is diverted to repair that\nitem — MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP (2) durability per point, held item first, then\nequipped armor — and only the remainder is banked.\n\nImplemented as one seam, `mendXp` in enchantments.ts, read once in `awardXp`, in\nkeeping with the one-reader-per-seam discipline. The event still reports the\ngross amount so the HUD and sound react to the full pickup. The `mending` id\nrides the existing per-slot `enchantments`, so no save-format bump is needed; it\nis added to the save validator's known-id set so it survives restore.\n\nThe fishing test's minimal GameState mock gains `equippedArmor`, which `awardXp`\nnow reads through the Mending seam.\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1",
  "description": "Commit 1: Mending enchantment"

52	  return {
53	    get length() {
54	      return data.size;
55	    },
56	    clear: () => data.clear(),
57	    getItem: (key: string) => data.get(key) ?? null,
58	    key: (index: number) => [...data.keys()][index] ?? null,
59	    removeItem: (key: string) => void data.delete(key),
60	    setItem: (key: string, value: string) => void data.set(key, value)
61	  };
62	}

3:## Schema
5:`SaveData` (version 10) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
14:- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
15:- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
27:Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
37:### Version history
39:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
40:- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
41:- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
42:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
43:- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
44:- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
45:- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
46:- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
47:- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
48:- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
49:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
50:- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
51:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10.
52:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
53:- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
56:- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).
58:## Profiles & worlds
60:Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):
66:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
72:### Legacy migration
76:## Autosave
80:## Compatibility rules
83:- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
84:- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.

1	# Save format & compatibility
2	
3	## Schema
4	
5	`SaveData` (version 10) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
6	
7	- world `seed`
8	- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
9	- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
10	- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
11	- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
12	- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
13	- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
14	- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
15	- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
16	- equipped armor
17	- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
18	- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
19	- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
20	- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
```

  "command": "git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nfeat(save): bump save format to v11 with per-item custom names\n\nThe upcoming anvil lets a player rename gear, which needs somewhere to persist\nthat name. This adds the storage layer ahead of the feature so the format change\nlands as its own reviewable, bisectable unit.\n\n`SavedSlot`/`InventorySlot` gain an optional `customName`; `SaveData` becomes v11\nwith a pure `migrateSaveV10toV11` bump, chained into `readSave`. The name is\nsnapshotted with the other per-slot fields and restored only on durable gear\n(the same population as enchantments and the rename feature), trimmed and capped\nto the new `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped, so a hand-edited blob can't\ninject an unbounded or whitespace name. Nothing writes `customName` yet — the\nanvil does that in a later commit — so this is additive and pre-v11 saves load\nunchanged.\n\nNo worldgen change (WORLDGEN_VERSION stays 8). Updates the save round-trip tests\n(final version 11, new custom-name cases) and the two engine tests that assert\nthe serialized version.\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -2",

}

258	export const ITEM_DEF_BY_ID: Record<string, ItemDef> = Object.fromEntries(ITEM_DEFS.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
259	
260	export function maxStackSizeForItem(itemId: string): number {
261	  return ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[itemId]?.maxDurability ? 1 : MAX_STACK_SIZE;
262	}
263	
264	export function createEmptySlot(): InventorySlot {
265	  return { id: null, label: "Empty", kind: null, count: 0 };
266	}
267	
268	export function createSlot(itemId: string, count: number): InventorySlot {
269	  const def = ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[itemId];
270	  if (!def) return createEmptySlot();
271	  const slot: InventorySlot = { ...def, count: Math.min(maxStackSizeForItem(itemId), Math.max(0, Math.floor(count))) };
272	  if ((def.kind === "tool" || def.kind === "weapon" || def.kind === "armor") && def.maxDurability) {
273	    slot.maxDurability = def.maxDurability;
274	    slot.durability = def.maxDurability;
275	  }
276	  return slot;
277	}
278	
279	export function createInitialInventory(): InventorySlot[] {
280	  const slots: InventorySlot[] = Array.from({ length: INVENTORY_SLOTS }, () => createEmptySlot());
281	  const starter: Array<{ id: string; count: number }> = [
282	    { id: "grass", count: 64 },
283	    { id: "dirt", count: 64 },
284	    { id: "stone", count: 64 },

291	  ];

{

  "content": "import { ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT, ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT, CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { ENCHANTMENT_DEFS } from \"@/lib/game/enchantments\";\nimport { REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport type { Enchantment, EnchantmentId, InventorySlot } from \"@/lib/game/types\";\n\n/**\n * Pure anvil logic: repairing, combining, and renaming durable gear. The engine\n * command handlers (GameEngine.dispatch) spend XP and mutate the inventory; these\n * helpers only compute the results, so they're trivially testable and side-effect\n * free. Durable gear is always count:1, so combine/repair never split a stack.\n */\n\n/** Whether a slot is durable gear the anvil can act on. */\nexport function isAnvilGear(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined): boolean {\n  return !!slot?.id && slot.count > 0 && !!slot.maxDurability && (slot.kind === \"tool\" || slot.kind === \"weapon\" || slot.kind === \"armor\");\n}\n\n/** Merge two enchant lists, taking the higher level per id, each capped at its def's maxLevel. */\nexport function mergeEnchantments(a: Enchantment[] = [], b: Enchantment[] = []): Enchantment[] {\n  const byId = new Map<EnchantmentId, number>();\n  for (const e of [...a, ...b]) byId.set(e.id, Math.max(byId.get(e.id) ?? 0, e.level));\n  const out: Enchantment[] = [];\n  for (const [id, level] of byId) out.push({ id, level: Math.min(ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[id].maxLevel, level) });\n  return out;\n}\n\n/** Index of another slot holding the same durable item id (count > 0), excluding `selectedSlot`; -1 if none. */\nexport function findSacrificeIndex(slots: InventorySlot[], selectedSlot: number): number {\n  const target = slots[selectedSlot];\n  if (!isAnvilGear(target)) return -1;\n  for (let i = 0; i < slots.length; i += 1) {\n    if (i === selectedSlot) continue;\n    const s = slots[i];\n    if (s.id === target.id && s.count > 0 && s.maxDurability) return i;\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\n/** True when combining would do real work — raise durability or add/raise an enchantment. */\nexport function wouldCombineHelp(target: InventorySlot, sacrifice: InventorySlot): boolean {\n  const max = target.maxDurability ?? 0;\n  const needsRepair = (target.durability ?? max) < max;\n  const merged = mergeEnchantments(target.enchantments, sacrifice.enchantments);\n  const grows = merged.some((e) => (target.enchantments?.find((t) => t.id === e.id)?.level ?? 0) < e.level);\n  return needsRepair || grows;\n}\n\n/** Merge a sacrifice into the target: combined durability + a bonus (capped), enchant union at the higher level. */\nexport function combineSlots(target: InventorySlot, sacrifice: InventorySlot): InventorySlot {\n  const max = target.maxDurability!;\n  const sum = (target.durability ?? max) + (sacrifice.durability ?? max) + Math.floor(max * ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT);\n  const enchantments = mergeEnchantments(target.enchantments, sacrifice.enchantments);\n  return { ...target, durability: Math.min(max, sum), enchantments: enchantments.length ? enchantments : undefined };\n}\n\n/** The material id that repairs a slot's gear, or undefined if it has none. */\nexport function repairMaterialFor(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined): string | undefined {\n  return slot?.id ? REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM[slot.id] : undefined;\n}\n\n/** Whether `slot` can be material-repaired now — it's damaged gear, has a repair material, and a unit is in stock. */\nexport function canMaterialRepair(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined, inventory: InventorySlot[]): boolean {\n  if (!isAnvilGear(slot)) return false;\n  const max = slot!.maxDurability!;\n  if ((slot!.durability ?? max) >= max) return false; // already full\n  const material = repairMaterialFor(slot);\n  if (!material) return false;\n  return inventory.some((s) => s.id === material && s.count > 0);\n}\n\n/** Restore a fixed fraction of max durability (one material unit's worth), capped at max. */\nexport function materialRepair(slot: InventorySlot): InventorySlot {\n  const max = slot.maxDurability!;\n  const restored = Math.ceil(max * ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT);\n  return { ...slot, durability: Math.min(max, (slot.durability ?? max) + restored) };\n}\n\n/** Trim and cap a requested custom name; \"\" means clear it. */\nexport function sanitizeCustomName(raw: string): string {\n  return raw.trim().slice(0, CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN);\n}\n"
}

31	export function adjustSlotCount(slots: InventorySlot[], slotId: string, delta: number, preferredIndex?: number): InventorySlot[] | null {
32	  if (!slotId || delta === 0) return null;
33	  const next = cloneSlots(slots);
34	  let remaining = Math.abs(delta);
35	
36	  if (delta < 0) {
37	    const consumeFromIndex = (index: number) => {
38	      if (remaining <= 0) return;
39	      if (index < 0 || index >= next.length) return;
40	      const slot = next[index];
41	      if (slot.id !== slotId || slot.count <= 0) return;
42	      const take = Math.min(remaining, slot.count);
43	      slot.count -= take;
44	      remaining -= take;
45	      if (slot.count <= 0) next[index] = createEmptySlot();
46	    };
47	
48	    if (typeof preferredIndex === "number") consumeFromIndex(preferredIndex);
49	    for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) consumeFromIndex(i);
50	    if (remaining > 0) return null;
51	    return next;
52	  }
53	
54	  if (!ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[slotId]) return null;
55	  const stackSize = maxStackSizeForItem(slotId);
56	
57	  const fillIndex = (index: number) => {
58	    if (remaining <= 0) return;
59	    if (index < 0 || index >= next.length) return;
60	    const slot = next[index];
61	    if (slot.id !== slotId || slot.count >= stackSize) return;
62	    const add = Math.min(remaining, stackSize - slot.count);
63	    slot.count += add;
64	    remaining -= add;
65	  };
66	
67	  if (typeof preferredIndex === "number") fillIndex(preferredIndex);
68	  for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) fillIndex(i);
69	  for (let i = 0; i < next.length && remaining > 0; i += 1) {
70	    if (next[i].id !== null || next[i].count !== 0) continue;
71	    const add = Math.min(remaining, stackSize);
72	    next[i] = createSlot(slotId, add);
73	    remaining -= add;
74	  }
75	  return next;
76	}
77	
78	/**
79	 * Wears the tool/weapon at `index` by `amount`; the slot empties at zero
80	 * durability. When `rng` is supplied, an Unbreaking enchant may skip the wear
81	 * (returning null — no change — like an inapplicable op).
82	 */

\"\"}`;\n  const [nameField, setNameField] = useState({ key: fieldKey, value: item?.customName ?? \"\" });\n  const name = nameField.key === fieldKey ? nameField.value : item?.customName ?? \"\";\n  const setName = (value: string) => setNameField({ key: fieldKey, value });\n\n  if (!gear || !item) {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"anvil-column\">\n        <div className=\"inventory-heading\">Anvil</div>\n        <div className=\"enchanting-hint\">Select a tool, weapon, or armor in the hotbar to repair or rename it.</div>\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  const max = item.maxDurability ?? ` with ${labelFor(material)}` : \"\"}</span>\n          <span className=\"enchant-cost\">{material ? `${repairCost} lvl` : \"—\"}</span>\n        </button>\n        <div className=\"anvil-status\">{repairStatus}</div>\n        <label className=\"anvil-rename-field\">\n          <span className=\"enchant-name\">Rename</span>\n          <input type=\"text\" value={name} maxLength={32} placeholder={item.label} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} aria-label=\"Custom item name\" />\n        </label>\n        <button className=\"anvil-action\" onClick={() => onRename(name)} disabled={!renameEnabled} aria-label={`Apply rename — costs ${renameCost} levels`}>\n          <span className=\"enchant-name\">{trimmed ? \"Apply name\" : \"Clear name\"}</span>\n          <span className=\"enchant-cost\">{renameCost} lvl</span>\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

1	"use client";
2	
3	import { type MouseEvent, useCallback, useState } from "react";
4	import { createPortal } from "react-dom";
5	import type { InventorySlot } from "@/lib/game/types";
6	
7	export type TooltipContent = { title: string; lines?: string[] } | null;
8	
9	/**
10	 * The tooltip content for an inventory slot, shared by the hotbar and the
11	 * inventory so both surfaces show the same details: the item label, plus a gray
12	 * "Durability x / y" line for damageable items. Empty slots get no tooltip.
13	 */
14	export function itemTooltipFor(slot: InventorySlot): TooltipContent {
15	  if (!slot.id || slot.count <= 0) return null;
16	  if (slot.maxDurability) {
17	    const lines = [`Durability ${slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability} / ${slot.maxDurability}`];
18	    if (slot.attack) lines.push(`Attack ${slot.attack}`);
19	    if (slot.meleeReach) lines.push(`Reach ${slot.meleeReach}`);
20	    if (slot.throwDamage) lines.push(`Throw damage ${slot.throwDamage}`);
21	    return { title: slot.label, lines };
22	  }
23	  return { title: slot.label };
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Minecraft-style item tooltip: a near-black box with a violet gradient border
28	 * that follows the cursor (matching the game and sidestepping clipping inside
29	 * the scrollable inventory). It renders in a portal on document.body and is
30	 * pointer-events:none, so it can never intercept the canvas click that
31	 * re-acquires pointer lock. During locked play the cursor is hidden and slots
32	 * aren't hover-reachable, so the tooltip simply never shows.
33	 *
34	 * Usage: `const { tooltip, bind } = useItemTooltip();` then spread
35	 * `{...bind(content)}` onto each hoverable element and render `{tooltip}` once.

1	/* eslint-disable @eslint-react/no-array-index-key -- the hotbar is a fixed-length, positional array of slots that never reorders, so the slot index is its stable identity */
2	import ItemIcon from "@/components/game/ItemIcon";
3	import { itemTooltipFor, useItemTooltip } from "@/components/game/ItemTooltip";
4	import type { InventorySlot } from "@/lib/game/types";
5	
6	type HotbarProps = {
7	  inventory: InventorySlot[];
8	  selectedSlot: number;
9	  hotbarSlots: number;
10	  onSelectSlot: (index: number) => void;
11	};
12	
13	/**
14	 * The Minecraft hotbar: 9 dark translucent slots with a white outline on the
15	 * selection and the selected item's name fading in above the bar. The name is
16	 * keyed on the selection so every change remounts it and replays the CSS
17	 * fade-in/fade-out animation — no timers or state.
18	 */
19	export default function Hotbar({ inventory, selectedSlot, hotbarSlots, onSelectSlot }: HotbarProps) {
20	  const visible = inventory.slice(0, hotbarSlots);
21	  const selected = visible[selectedSlot];
22	  const selectedLabel = selected?.id && selected.count > 0 ? selected.label : "";
23	  const { tooltip, bind } = useItemTooltip();
24	
25	  return (
26	    <div className="hotbar-area">
27	      {selectedLabel && (
28	        <div key={`${selectedSlot}:${selectedLabel}`} className="hotbar-item-name">
29	          {selectedLabel}
30	        </div>
31	      )}
32	      <div className="hotbar" data-testid="hotbar">
33	        {visible.map((slot, idx) => (
34	          <button
35	            key={`hotbar-${idx}`}
36	            className={idx === selectedSlot ? "hotbar-slot active" : "hotbar-slot"}
37	            onClick={() => onSelectSlot(idx)}
38	            aria-label={slot.id && slot.count > 0 ? `Slot ${idx + 1}: ${slot.label}` : `Slot ${idx + 1}: empty`}
39	            {...bind(itemTooltipFor(slot))}
40	          >

336	over it. You gain XP for **killing mobs** (tougher mobs give more — the boss is a
337	big payout), **mining ores** (rarer ores give more), and **reeling in fish**. XP
338	is a currency, so unlike potion effects it **stays with you when you die**.
339	
340	Spend it at an **enchanting table** (craft one from **2 diamond ore + 4 cobble**).
341	Place it, right-click to open the enchanting panel, then **select** the tool,
342	weapon, or armor you want to improve in your hotbar — the panel shows the
343	enchantments it can take. Each costs **3 levels** and can be applied up to **three
344	times**:
345	
346	- **Sharpness** (weapons) — hit harder in melee
347	- **Protection** (armor) — take less damage
348	- **Efficiency** (tools) — mine faster
349	- **Unbreaking** (any gear) — gear lasts longer (it sometimes ignores wear)
350	- **Mending** (any gear) — XP you pick up repairs the held or worn item instead of
351	  banking, as long as it's damaged
352	
353	Buttons grey out when you can't afford the cost or the enchant is maxed.
354	Enchantments are part of the item, so they're kept in chests and across reloads.
355	Full numbers are in the [reference](reference.md#xp--enchanting).
356

The result keeps the best of\n  both: its durability is restored (the two bars added together, plus a bonus) and\n  any enchantments are merged, taking the higher level of each. 5:## A new block
7:1. Add to the `BlockId` enum and `BLOCK_COLORS` in `lib/world/blocks.ts` — the atlas auto-generates its tile. Add a `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` entry for the first-person model tint.
9:3. Make it placeable/droppable: an `ITEM_DEFS` entry (`kind: "block"`, `blockId`) plus a `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` mapping — without the mapping, mining it drops nothing. The inventory icon (isometric cube) auto-generates from `BLOCK_COLORS`; ore-style blocks can add an accent color in `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts` (`ORE_ACCENTS`).
12:6. Map it to a sound family in `lib/game/audio/materials.ts` — the `BlockId → MaterialGroup` record is exhaustive, so typecheck fails until the entry exists.
16:## A new item or recipe
30:- Recipes are `{ id, label, cost: [{slotId, count}], result: {slotId, count} }` in `lib/game/recipes.ts`. An optional `station` makes a recipe station-gated: it only crafts while that station's panel is open, enforced in the `craft` command and shown locked in the recipe book. The stations are `"furnace"` (smelting), `"villager"` (a **trade** — see below), and `"brewing"` (potions, opened at a brewing stand). Adding a station means extending that union in **four** places (`Recipe.station` in `types.ts`, `craftingStation` on both `GameState` and `GameSnapshot` in `state.ts`, and the `openedStation` event), plus a `RecipeCategory` + a `recipeCategory()` branch and a `STATION_LABELS` entry (`InventoryPanel.tsx`).
31:- **Villager trades** (`lib/game/trades.ts`) ARE just `station: "villager"` recipes spread into `RECIPES`, so they reuse the whole crafting pipeline and recipe-book UI for free. To open them, an interaction sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` (right-clicking a villager via `tryTradeAimedVillager` in `interact.ts`); the panel then shows the trades as a **Trading** book and the `craft` command runs them. Emerald is the currency — add sell offers (material → emerald) and buy offers (emerald → goods) to keep the economy two-sided. There's no persisted trade state, so this needs no save-format change.
35:## A new mob drop
40:## A new mob
50:## A ranged weapon or ranged mob
57:## An explosion (creeper, TNT, or anything that blows up)
64:## A new player skin preset
70:## A new sound
76:## An interactive block (right-click behavior)
78:- Right-click (and KeyE) dispatch `placeBlock`, which runs a fixed precedence in `GameEngine.dispatch` before falling through to placement: feed an aimed mob → `tryInteractBlock` → use the held item → place. To make a block do something on right-click, register it in `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` and add a branch in `tryInteractBlock` (`lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`).
80:- Four reference implementations: the **door** atomically toggles matching upper/lower state IDs; the **bed** sets `state.spawnPoint` and starts the sleep fade (`state.sleepTimer`); the **furnace** opens the inventory and sets `state.craftingStation`, which unlocks its `station` recipes (see "A new item or recipe"); the **chest** opens the inventory and sets `state.openContainerIndex` (see below). A block that opens the inventory from a mouse click also needs an `openedStation`/`openedContainer` handler in `useMinecraftGame` to release pointer lock. See [architecture.md](architecture.md) for the step order.
82:## A container block (block-entity storage)
84:- Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, so any block that needs **attached data** (a chest's items) stores it in `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>`, keyed by `world.index(x,y,z)`. The chest is the reference:
85:  - **Open**: `interactChest` (an `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` branch) lazily creates the slot array, sets `state.openContainerIndex`, opens the inventory, and emits `openedContainer`. The snapshot exposes `container`, and `InventoryPanel` renders a second grid; `toggleInventory`/`pause` clear `openContainerIndex`.
90:## A random-tick behavior (growth / spread)
92:- Block updates that happen "over time" run through `lib/game/engine/systems/randomTicks.ts`: every `RANDOM_TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` it samples `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES` columns within `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS` of the player and runs a handler on each column's top block. Register a `BlockId → handler` in `RANDOM_TICK_HANDLERS`; the handler edits via `state.blockChanges` and sets `state.worldMeshDirty`.
95:- A growing block also needs the usual block plumbing — a `BlockId` (appended at the end of the enum so saved ids don't shift), `BLOCK_COLORS` + an atlas paint branch (plants reuse the wheat trick: a solid cube painted to read as a plant, so no new geometry), an exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` sound entry, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/`rollBlockDrops`. A new **material** item (e.g. bone meal) must also get an `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS` entry, or the sprite test fails its no-magenta-checker assertion.
98:## A transient (session-only) entity (projectile, bobber, …)
104:## A worldgen structure (houses, dungeons, …)
110:## A loot table / lazy block-entity fill
115:## A status effect (timed buff / hazard)
124:## An enchantment (per-item gear modifier)
132:## A new mechanic
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/grindstone.ts",
  "content": "import { GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport type { InventorySlot } from \"@/lib/game/types\";\n\n/**\n * Pure grindstone logic: removing enchantments from durable gear in exchange for\n * an XP refund. Like the anvil helpers, this only computes results — the engine\n * command spends/banks XP and mutates the inventory.\n */\n\n/** Total enchantment levels on a slot (0 if none). */\nexport function totalEnchantLevels(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined): number {\n  return slot?.enchantments?.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.level, 0) ?? 0;\n}\n\n/** Whether the grindstone can act on a slot — it carries at least one enchantment. */\nexport function canStripEnchantments(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined): boolean {\n  return totalEnchantLevels(slot) > 0;\n}\n\n/** XP points refunded for stripping a slot's enchantments. */\nexport function enchantRefund(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined): number {\n  return totalEnchantLevels(slot) * GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL;\n}\n\n/** A copy of the slot with all enchantments removed. */\nexport function stripEnchantments(slot: InventorySlot): InventorySlot {\n  return { ...slot, enchantments: undefined };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import ItemIcon from \"@/components/game/ItemIcon\";\nimport { ENCHANTMENT_DEFS, enchantLevel } from \"@/lib/game/enchantments\";\nimport { canStripEnchantments, enchantRefund } from \"@/lib/game/grindstone\";\nimport { displayName } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport type { InventorySlot } from \"@/lib/game/types\";\n\ntype GrindstoneColumnProps = {\n  /** The selected hotbar item to disenchant (or undefined/empty). */\n  item: InventorySlot | undefined;\n  onStrip: () => void;\n};\n\nconst ROMAN = [\"\", \"I\", \"II\", \"III\", \"IV\", \"V\"];\n\n/**\n * The grindstone panel (replaces the recipe book while a grindstone is open):\n * strips every enchantment off the selected hotbar gear, refunding XP. Mirrors\n * the enchanting/anvil panels — it acts on whichever hotbar slot is selected.\n */\nexport default function GrindstoneColumn({ item, onStrip }: GrindstoneColumnProps) {\n  const strippable = canStripEnchantments(item);\n\n  if (!item || !strippable) {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"anvil-column\">\n        <div className=\"inventory-heading\">Grindstone</div>\n        <div className=\"enchanting-hint\">Select an enchanted tool, weapon, or armor in the hotbar to remove its enchantments for XP.</div>\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  const refund = enchantRefund(item);\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"anvil-column\">\n      <div className=\"inventory-heading\">Grindstone</div>\n      <div className=\"enchanting-item\">\n        <ItemIcon slot={item} size={32} />\n        <span>{displayName(item)}</span>\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"enchanting-cost\">Removing returns +{refund} XP</div>\n      <div className=\"anvil-actions\">\n        <div className=\"grindstone-enchants\">\n          {item.enchantments?.map((e) => (\n            <div key={e.id} className=\"grindstone-enchant\">\n              {ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[e.id].label}\n              {enchantLevel(item, e.id) ? ` ${ROMAN[e.level]}` : \"\"}\n            </div>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n        <button className=\"anvil-action\" onClick={onStrip} aria-label={`Remove enchantments — returns ${refund} XP`}>\n          <span className=\"enchant-name\">Remove enchantments</span>\n          <span className=\"enchant-cost\">+{refund} XP</span>\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/grindstone.test.ts",
  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport { GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { canStripEnchantments, enchantRefund, stripEnchantments, totalEnchantLevels } from \"@/lib/game/grindstone\";\nimport { createSlot } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport type { Enchantment, InventorySlot } from \"@/lib/game/types\";\n\nconst withEnchants = (id: string, ...e: Enchantment[]): InventorySlot => ({ ...createSlot(id, 1), enchantments: e });\nconst ench = (id: string, level: number): Enchantment => ({ id: id as never, level });\n\ndescribe(\"grindstone\", () => {\n  test(\"totalEnchantLevels sums every enchantment's level\", () => {\n    expect(totalEnchantLevels(createSlot(\"diamond_sword\", 1))).toBe(0);\n    expect(totalEnchantLevels(withEnchants(\"diamond_sword\", ench(\"sharpness\", 3), ench(\"unbreaking\", 1)))).toBe(4);\n  });\n\n  test(\"canStripEnchantments is true only when enchantments are present\", () => {\n    expect(canStripEnchantments(withEnchants(\"diamond_sword\", ench(\"sharpness\", 1)))).toBe(true);\n    expect(canStripEnchantments(createSlot(\"diamond_sword\", 1))).toBe(false);\n    expect(canStripEnchantments(createSlot(\"dirt\", 1))).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  test(\"enchantRefund scales with total levels\", () => {\n    expect(enchantRefund(withEnchants(\"diamond_sword\", ench(\"sharpness\", 3), ench(\"unbreaking\", 1)))).toBe(4 * GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL);\n  });\n\n  test(\"stripEnchantments clears enchantments immutably\", () => {\n    const before = withEnchants(\"diamond_sword\", ench(\"sharpness\", 2));\n    const after = stripEnchantments(before);\n    expect(after.enchantments).toBeUndefined();\n    expect(before.enchantments).toHaveLength(1); // original untouched\n  });\n});\n"
}

136	## XP & enchanting
137	
138	`XP_PER_LEVEL`, `FISHING_XP`, `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`, `ENCHANT_COST_LEVELS`,
139	`SHARPNESS_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL`, `PROTECTION_DEFENSE_PER_LEVEL`,
140	`EFFICIENCY_SPEED_PER_LEVEL`, `UNBREAKING_SKIP_PER_LEVEL`, `MENDING_MAX_LEVEL`,
141	`MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP`.
142	
143	XP banks as points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` (10) points make one level. The per-mob and
144	per-ore XP tables live in `mobXp.ts` / `systems/xp.ts` (not here, like
145	`mobLoot.ts`); `FISHING_XP` (2) is the per-catch reward. Enchanting costs
146	`ENCHANT_COST_LEVELS` (3) levels per application, up to `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL` (3).
147	Each enchant is a flat per-level modifier read at one seam:
148	Sharpness `+SHARPNESS_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL` (2) melee damage (`combat.ts` dispatch),
149	Protection `+PROTECTION_DEFENSE_PER_LEVEL` (2) defense (`equippedDefense` →
150	`armorReduction`), Efficiency `×(1 + EFFICIENCY_SPEED_PER_LEVEL × level)` mining
151	speed (`miningSpeed`), Unbreaking a `UNBREAKING_SKIP_PER_LEVEL` (0.2)
152	skip-chance per level (`consumeToolDurability`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability`),
153	and Mending (`MENDING_MAX_LEVEL` 1, binary) diverting gained XP to repair
154	`MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` (2) durability per point on the held/worn item (`mendXp`,
155	read once in `awardXp`). Lower the costs or raise the magnitudes for faster
156	progression; the XP-source tables are the earning dial.
157

Lower the costs or raise the magnitudes for faster\nprogression; the XP-source tables are the earning dial.\n\n## Anvil & grindstone\n\n`ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS`, `ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS`, `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS`,\n`ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT`, `ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT`, `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`,\n`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL`.\n\nThe anvil spends XP levels to maintain gear (`lib/game/anvil.ts`, applied in\n`GameEngine.dispatch`): **combine** a duplicate for `ANVIL_COMBINE_COST_LEVELS` (4) —\nthe two durabilities add together plus a `ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT` (0.12 × max) bonus,\nand enchantments merge at the higher level; **material repair** for\n`ANVIL_REPAIR_COST_LEVELS` (1) restores `ANVIL_MATERIAL_REPAIR_PCT` (0.25 × max)\ndurability per material unit; **rename** for `ANVIL_RENAME_COST_LEVELS` (1) sets a\ncustom name capped at `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` (32). The grindstone is the inverse — it\n**strips** all enchantments and refunds `GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP points\nper level removed (`lib/game/grindstone.ts`). Raise the repair percentages or lower\nthe costs to make upkeep cheaper; raise the grindstone refund to make disenchanting\nmore rewarding. The repair-material map (which material mends which gear) lives in\n`REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM` in `items.ts`."

> AGENT

Done. The **Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression** feature is fully implemented on branch `feat/anvil-grindstone-mending`, working tree clean.

## What landed (5 commits)

1. **`feat(enchanting): add Mending enchantment`** — a 5th enchantment at the existing table; gained XP repairs held/worn gear via a single `mendXp` seam in `awardXp`.
2. **`feat(save): bump save format to v11`** — per-item `customName`, pure v10→v11 migration, restored durable-only and sanitized.
3. **`feat(anvil): … repairing, combining, and renaming gear`** — new craft-only Anvil block; combine a duplicate (durability + merged enchants), material repair, and rename, all on the selected hotbar item for XP.
4. **`feat(grindstone): … strip enchantments for XP`** — new craft-only Grindstone block; removes all enchants and refunds XP.
5. **`test(e2e): expect save version 11`** — reconciled the reload smoke test with the v11 bump.

## Verification — all green
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `build` ✓
- `bun test` — **820 pass / 0 fail** (added: `anvil`, `grindstone`, `AnvilColumn`, `GrindstoneColumn` suites + engine, save, recipe, mending/xp cases)
- `bun run test:e2e` — **17 passed**

Each commit is bisectable (green on the unit gate), has a "why" body, and ships its own docs (`manual`, `reference`, `tuning`, `save-format`, `adding-content`) + `CHANGELOG`. No `Co-Authored-By` trailers, no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump (both blocks are craft-only).

A few defaults worth a glance in review (all easy `config.ts` tunables): recipe costs (Anvil = 3 gold ore + 4 cobble, Grindstone = 2 cobble + 2 planks), XP costs (combine 4 / repair 1 / rename 1), repair percentages, and the grindstone refund (5 XP/level).

Per your usual flow I've left everything committed locally and **haven't pushed or opened the PR** — that's yours to kick off when you've looked it over. When you're ready: `gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`.

81	- **A station with its own panel (not the recipe book)** — the **enchanting table** and the **anvil** are the reference. Their interaction sets `state.craftingStation` to a new id, but that id goes on the **engine/UI** station union (`craftingStation` on `GameState` and `GameSnapshot`, and the `openedStation` event in `state.ts`, plus the `InventoryPanel` `craftingStation` prop) and **not** on `Recipe.station` — so `STATION_LABELS` (keyed off `Recipe.station`) needs no entry. The panel is a dedicated `*Column` component branched in before the recipe book in `InventoryPanel`, acting on the **selected hotbar slot** (`inventory[selectedHotbarSlot]`); its actions are new `Command`s in `commands.ts` handled in `GameEngine.dispatch` (gated on `state.craftingStation === <id>`), each emitting a one-shot event for the audio director. The block itself is **craft-only** (never generated), so adding the `BlockId` at the end of the enum needs **no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump** — just `BLOCK_COLORS` (atlas sizing), an atlas paint branch, the exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK`, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/item-def/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/recipe.

2	import ItemIcon from "@/components/game/ItemIcon";
3	import { canMaterialRepair, findSacrificeIndex, isAnvilGear, repairMaterialFor, wouldCombineHelp } from "@/lib/game/anvil";
4	import { displayName, ITEM_DEF_BY_ID } from "@/lib/game/items";
5	import type { InventorySlot } from "@/lib/game/types";
6	
7	type AnvilColumnProps = {
8	  /** The selected hotbar item to repair/combine/rename (or undefined/empty). */
9	  item: InventorySlot | undefined;
10	  /** Full inventory, to detect a combine duplicate and the repair material. */
11	  inventory: InventorySlot[];
12	  selectedHotbarSlot: number;
13	  xpLevel: number;
14	  combineCost: number;
15	  repairCost: number;
16	  renameCost: number;
17	  onCombine: () => void;
18	  onRepair: () => void;
19	  onRename: (name: string) => void;
20	};
21	
22	const labelFor = (slotId: string): string => ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[slotId]?.label ?? slotId;
23	
24	/**
25	 * The anvil panel (replaces the recipe book while an anvil is open): repair,
26	 * combine, or rename the selected hotbar gear, each spending XP levels. Mirrors
27	 * the enchanting panel — it acts on whichever hotbar slot is selected.
28	 */
29	export default function AnvilColumn({
30	  item,
31	  inventory,
32	  selectedHotbarSlot,
33	  xpLevel,
34	  combineCost,
35	  repairCost,
36	  renameCost,
37	  onCombine,
38	  onRepair,
39	  onRename
40	}: AnvilColumnProps) {
41	  const gear = isAnvilGear(item);
42	  // Reset the rename field whenever the targeted item changes.
43	  const fieldKey = `${selectedHotbarSlot}:${item?.id ?? ""}`;
44	  const [nameField, setNameField] = useState({ key: fieldKey, value: item?.customName ?? "" });
45	  const name = nameField.key === fieldKey ? nameField.value : (item?.customName ?? "");
46	  const setName = (value: string) => setNameField({ key: fieldKey, value });
47	
48	  if (!gear || !item) {
49	    return (
50	      <div className="anvil-column">
51	        <div className="inventory-heading">Anvil</div>
52	        <div className="enchanting-hint">Select a tool, weapon, or armor in the hotbar to repair or rename it.</div>
53	      </div>
54	    );
55	  }
56	
57	  const max = item.maxDurability ?? 0;
58	  const durability = item.durability ?? max;
59	
60	  const sacrificeIndex = findSacrificeIndex(inventory, selectedHotbarSlot);
61	  const hasDuplicate = sacrificeIndex >= 0;
62	  const combineHelps = hasDuplicate && wouldCombineHelp(item, inventory[sacrificeIndex]);
63	  const combineEnabled = combineHelps && xpLevel >= combineCost;
64	  const combineStatus = !hasDuplicate
65	    ? `Need a second ${displayName(item)} to combine`
66	    : !combineHelps
67	      ? "Already at full durability and enchantments"
68	      : xpLevel < combineCost
69	        ? "Not enough XP"
70	        : `Costs ${combineCost} levels`;
71	
72	  const material = repairMaterialFor(item);
73	  const repairable = canMaterialRepair(item, inventory);
74	  const repairEnabled = repairable && xpLevel >= repairCost;
75	  const repairStatus = !material
76	    ? "No repair material for this item"
77	    : durability >= max
78	      ? "Already at full durability"
79	      : !repairable
80	        ? `Need ${labelFor(material)} to repair`
81	        : xpLevel < repairCost
82	          ? "Not enough XP"
83	          : `Costs ${repairCost} levels`;
84	
85	  const trimmed = name.trim();
86	  const renameChanged = trimmed !== (item.customName ?? "");
87	  const renameEnabled = renameChanged && xpLevel >= renameCost;
88	
89	  return (
90	    <div className="anvil-column">
91	      <div className="inventory-heading">Anvil</div>
92	      <div className="enchanting-item">
93	        <ItemIcon slot={item} size={32} />
94	        <span>{displayName(item)}</span>
95	      </div>
96	      <div className="enchanting-cost">
97	        Durability {durability} / {max} · you have {xpLevel} levels
98	      </div>
99	      <div className="anvil-actions">
100	        <button className="anvil-action" onClick={onCombine} disabled={!combineEnabled} aria-label={`Combine duplicate — ${combineStatus}`}>
101	          <span className="enchant-name">Combine duplicate</span>
102	          <span className="enchant-cost">{hasDuplicate ? `${combineCost} lvl` : "—"}</span>
103	        </button>
104	        <div className="anvil-status">{combineStatus}</div>
105	        <button className="anvil-action" onClick={onRepair} disabled={!repairEnabled} aria-label={`Repair with material — ${repairStatus}`}>
106	          <span className="enchant-name">Repair{material ? ` with ${labelFor(material)}` : ""}</span>
107	          <span className="enchant-cost">{material ? `${repairCost} lvl` : "—"}</span>
108	        </button>
109	        <div className="anvil-status">{repairStatus}</div>
110	        <label className="anvil-rename-field">
111	          <span className="enchant-name">Rename</span>
112	          <input type="text" value={name} maxLength={32} placeholder={item.label} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} aria-label="Custom item name" />
113	        </label>
114	        <button className="anvil-action" onClick={() => onRename(name)} disabled={!renameEnabled} aria-label={`Apply rename — costs ${renameCost} levels`}>
115	          <span className="enchant-name">{trimmed ? "Apply name" : "Clear name"}</span>
116	          <span className="enchant-cost">{renameCost} lvl</span>
117	        </button>
118	      </div>
119	    </div>
120	  );
121	}
122

CodeRabbit posted **9 actionable comments**. I triaged them, applied the valid ones, and committed the fixes locally (not pushed — your call to review first).

## Applied (6)

| Fix | What |
|---|---|
| **save: per-enchant clamp** | `restoreEnchantments` now clamps each enchant to its *own* max, so a tampered `mending:3` save loads as level 1 (was clamped to the global `ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL` of 3). + regression test. |
| **anvil rename field** | Reset key now includes the saved name (swapping a same-id item with a different name refreshes the field), submit is sanitized, input cap uses `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`. |
| **docs/reference** | Fixed the self-contradiction — intro now says "per-enchant max (3 for most, 1 for Mending)" instead of a flat "level 3". |
| **docs/adding-content** | Dedicated-panel guidance now names the grindstone alongside enchanting/anvil. |
| **test type-safety** | New `ench`/`enchanted` helpers use `EnchantmentId` instead of `id as never` (anvil, grindstone, GrindstoneColumn tests). |
| **test constant** | Combine-bonus assertion uses `ANVIL_REPAIR_BONUS_PCT` instead of a hard-coded `0.12`. |

## Declined (3), with rationale

- **"EquippedArmor needs a per-instance key"** (3 comments: InventoryPanel, mendXp, types). This is **pre-existing, not introduced here** — `equippedDefense`, `armorReduction`, and `consumeEquippedArmorDurability` have *always* resolved equipped armor by `findIndex(slot.id === id)`, and per-instance enchantments shipped back in v7. My `mendXp` just follows that established pattern. Fixing it properly means changing the persisted `equippedArmor` shape plus all four armor seams — a cross-cutting refactor that's out of scope for this PR and worth a dedicated follow-up. I noted this in the commit body.
- **`as unknown as GameState` test fixture** — matches the repo-wide test pattern (`fishing.test.ts`, `combat.test.ts`, etc.); a fully-typed `GameState` fixture is disproportionate here.

1	# Anvil, Grindstone & Gear Progression
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The game shipped XP + an **Enchanting Table** (4 enchantments, applied to the selected
6	hotbar item) and Hardcore mode. The natural completion of that progression arc is gear
7	*maintenance and consolidation*: a way to repair worn gear, merge enchantments, rename
8	items, auto-repair from XP, and strip enchantments back for a refund. This plan adds:
9	
10	- **Anvil** — repair worn gear two ways (same-item **combine**, which also merges
11	  enchantments; and **material repair**, consuming the gear's tier material), plus
12	  **rename**. Costs XP levels.
13	- **Grindstone** — strip all enchantments off an item, refunding some XP.
14	- **Mending** enchantment — applied at the *existing* Enchanting Table; passively
15	  diverts gained XP to repair the held/worn gear that carries it.
```

Perfect! Now I have all the evidence. Let me compile the complete investigation report.

---

## Investigation Report: Armor Occupying Hotbar Slot

### 1. How Armor is Equipped — `toggleEquipArmor()`

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/inventory.ts` (lines 269–276)

```typescript
/** Toggles the armor piece at `index` in its armor slot. */
export function toggleEquipArmor(slots: InventorySlot[], equipped: EquippedArmor, index: number): EquippedArmor | null {
  if (index < 0 || index >= slots.length) return null;
  const slot = slots[index];
  if (slot.kind !== "armor" || !slot.id || !slot.armorSlot || slot.count <= 0) return null;
  const next = { ...equipped };
  next[slot.armorSlot] = equipped[slot.armorSlot] === slot.id ? null : slot.id;
  return next;
}
```

**Critical finding:** The armor item is **NOT removed** from the inventory. The function only toggles the item's **ID reference** in the `equippedArmor` object. The original inventory slot object remains untouched and stays in its index position. The actual item object persists in the `slots` array.

---

### 2. The `EquippedArmor` Data Model

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/types.ts` (line 8)

```typescript
export type EquippedArmor = Record<ArmorSlot, string | null>;
```

**Structure:** `EquippedArmor` is a by-ID reference map, not a slot container:
- Maps armor slot names (e.g., `"helmet"`, `"chestplate"`) to item IDs (string) or `null`
- Example: `{ helmet: "iron_helmet_id_001", chestplate: null, … }`
- **The item itself lives in the main 36-slot inventory array**, stored by index position
- Equipped armor is purely a pointer: it doesn't move the item or create a separate storage area
- When you unequip, the item stays where it was; the reference is cleared to `null`

---

### 3. The Hotbar Rendering

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/Hotbar.tsx` (line 21)

```typescript
const visible = inventory.slice(0, hotbarSlots);
```

**Critical:** The hotbar directly shows the first 9 (or configured `hotbarSlots`) inventory slots via a slice. If an armor item is equipped and lives in slot 0–8, **it still renders visually in the hotbar** because the slice includes it and the hotbar renders all items in its range, regardless of whether they're equipped.

---

### 4. The Inventory Armor Column Display

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` (lines 211–232)

```typescript
const equippedId = equippedArmor[armorSlot];
const equippedIndex = equippedId ? inventory.findIndex((slot) => slot.id === equippedId && slot.count > 0) : -1;
const equippedItem = equippedIndex >= 0 ? inventory[equippedIndex] : undefined;
```

**Critical finding:** The armor column finds the equipped item by doing a **linear search through the entire inventory array** (`inventory.findIndex()`). This means:
- The equipped item is rendered in the **armor column (left side of inventory panel)**
- The **same item object is also rendered in its original inventory/hotbar slot** (if in slots 0–8 or 9–35)
- A single armor piece appears **in two places simultaneously**: in the armor column AND in its original inventory position

This is the bug: an equipped armor piece occupies visual space in both the armor column and (if it was in slots 0–8) the hotbar.

---

### 5. Is This Pre-Existing or Recently Introduced?

**Git blame for `toggleEquipArmor`:**  
All lines were added in commit `0a3e599` on **2026-06-11 16:12:26**.

**Commit message:** `Extract pure inventory operations into lib/game/inventory.ts`

**Recent anvil/grindstone/mending work:**
```
f8b0ddc (2026-06-28) fix(review): address CodeRabbit feedback on gear-progression PR
beb3781 (2026-06-28) feat(grindstone): add Grindstone to strip enchantments for XP
613167d (2026-06-28) feat(anvil): add Anvil for repairing, combining, and renaming gear
861ed71 (2026-06-28) feat(save): bump save format to v11 with per-item custom names
c61a2dd (2026-06-28) feat(enchanting): add Mending enchantment
```

**Verification:** `git diff 0a3e599..613167d -- lib/game/inventory.ts` shows **zero modifications** to `toggleEquipArmor`, `EquippedArmor`, or any armor-related functions between the original extraction and today's commits.

**Verdict:** This is a **PRE-EXISTING design**, introduced on 2026-06-11 (17 days ago) and untouched by recent work. The armor-by-reference system was built into the initial extraction and never modified.

---

### 6. Intended Design According to Docs

**From `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/docs/reference.md`:**
```
Each piece occupies its own equip slot. Defense reduces incoming damage (a hit always deals at least 1).
```

**From `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` (lines 234–238):**
```typescript
<div className="inventory-hint">
  Click one slot, then another to move items.
  <br />
  Click armor to equip or unequip it.
</div>
```

**From architecture docs:** No explicit documentation of how equipped armor should interact with inventory slots.

**Gap:** The docs mention "equip slot" (suggesting dedicated storage) but the code implements by-reference with the item remaining in the main inventory. The UI hint "Click armor to equip or unequip it" suggests a toggle interaction, which matches the current code, but doesn't clarify whether the item should stay in inventory or move to a dedicated armor container.

---

## Clear Verdict

**Is "equipped armor occupies a hotbar slot" the current intended design?**  
**YES.** The current by-reference design intentionally stores equipped armor items in the main inventory array and only maintains a pointer in `EquippedArmor`. This means:
- An equipped item from slots 0–8 **will render in the hotbar**
- The same item **also renders in the armor column** (rendering it twice)
- This is not a bug in the implementation—the code does exactly what it was designed to do

**Is it pre-existing or newly introduced?**  
**PRE-EXISTING.** Introduced on 2026-06-11 in the "Extract pure inventory operations" commit. Untouched by all recent anvil/grindstone/mending work.

**However,** this design conflicts with real Minecraft behavior (where equipped armor moves to dedicated slots and frees the hotbar) and may not be the *intended* player experience. The bug report suggests the player expects armor to occupy only the armor column, not the hotbar—which would require a redesign to move equipped items out of the main inventory array into a dedicated armor container.

> AGENT

I've diagnosed it. Here's my assessment:

**This is a real UX problem, but it's pre-existing — not from my recent PR.** The armor system equips *by reference*: `toggleEquipArmor` just sets `equippedArmor[slot] = item.id` and leaves the actual item sitting in its inventory slot (`inventory.ts:269`). So:
- An equipped helmet that lives in a hotbar slot keeps occupying that hotbar slot.
- The same piece renders **twice** — once in the hotbar/inventory grid, once in the armor column.
- This has been the behavior since the inventory module was extracted (2026‑06‑11); none of the anvil/grindstone/mending commits touched it.

The docs even claim "each piece occupies its own equip slot," which the code doesn't actually implement — so fixing it aligns code with intent.

The clean fix is **dedicated armor storage**: equipping *moves* the piece out of inventory into its armor slot (freeing the hotbar/inventory slot, killing the double-render). That's the Minecraft model — and as a bonus it eliminates the by-id ambiguity CodeRabbit flagged on the PR. It's a cross-cutting change though (the `equippedArmor` model, the combat/durability/mending seams, save format → v12, and the inventory UI), so I want to confirm scope before planning it.

A couple of decisions that change what I plan:

# Implementation Plan: Armor Dedicated Storage (save v12)

## Summary of the bug and the fix
Today `EquippedArmor = Record<ArmorSlot, string | null>` (`lib/game/types.ts:8`) is a by-id marker; the worn item physically stays in `state.inventory`, so it renders in both the armor column and its hotbar/storage slot. Every armor seam re-locates the item with `slots.find(s => s.id === equippedId)`, which is also ambiguous when two identical pieces exist. The fix moves the actual `InventorySlot` instance into the record, so equipping vacates the inventory slot and there is one canonical store for each worn piece.

This is additive-with-transform on the save (v11 → v12) and touches no worldgen, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8 and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** (`lib/game/config.ts:265`).

---

## 1. Type + model change

**`lib/game/types.ts`**
- Change the runtime type (line 8):
  `export type EquippedArmor = Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>;`
  (`InventorySlot` is declared lower at line 41; alias forward-reference is fine.)
- **Critical decoupling of the saved shape from the runtime type.** `SaveDataV1.equippedArmor` is currently `Partial<EquippedArmor>` (line 100) and is inherited by every later `SaveDataVx` via `Omit`. Once `EquippedArmor` means "instances", that field's type would silently change for legacy saves, which is wrong (old saves stored string ids). Introduce two dedicated saved types and stop referencing the runtime type from the save shapes:
  - `export type SavedArmorById = Partial<Record<ArmorSlot, string | null>>;` (legacy v1–v11)
  - `export type SavedEquippedArmor = Partial<Record<ArmorSlot, SavedSlot>>;` (v12+; reuses the existing `SavedSlot` at line 88, which already carries `durability`/`enchantments`/`customName`)
  - Retype `SaveDataV1.equippedArmor?: SavedArmorById` (line 100).
- Add v12 to the version chain (replace the current `SaveData` at lines 211–213):
  - Rename current to `export type SaveDataV11 = Omit<SaveDataV10, "version"> & { version: 11 };`
  - `export type SaveData = Omit<SaveDataV11, "version" | "equippedArmor"> & { version: 12; equippedArmor?: SavedEquippedArmor };`

**`lib/game/items.ts`**
- `createEmptyArmorEquipment()` (line 27) returns all-`null`, which is valid for both the old and new type — only its return type changes. No body change.

**Ripple to snapshot/prop types** (no structural change, the named type just now means instances):
- `lib/game/engine/state.ts:152` (`GameState.equippedArmor`) and `:275` (`GameSnapshot.equippedArmor`) keep `EquippedArmor`.
- `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx:20` prop keeps `EquippedArmor`.
