## 2. Inventory seams — `lib/game/inventory.ts`

**`toggleEquipArmor` (rewrite, line 269)** — now MOVES the piece and returns both arrays. Proposed shape:
```
export function toggleEquipArmor(slots, equipped, index):
  { slots: InventorySlot[]; equipped: EquippedArmor } | null
```
- Guard `index`, `slot.kind === "armor"`, `slot.id`, `slot.armorSlot`, `count > 0` (unchanged guards).
- `armorSlot = slot.armorSlot`; clone slots (`cloneSlots`) and the record (`{ ...equipped }`).
- `previouslyWorn = equipped[armorSlot]`; set `nextEquipped[armorSlot] = { ...slot, count: 1 }`; set `nextSlots[index] = previouslyWorn ? { ...previouslyWorn } : createEmptySlot()`.
- This makes "equip" also a swap when that armor slot is already filled (the worn piece lands in the vacated grid index). Because a worn piece is no longer in the grid, the old click-to-toggle-off behaviour from the grid disappears — that is intended; un-equip is now a separate command (below).

**`unequipArmor` (new)**:
```
export function unequipArmor(slots, equipped, armorSlot):
  { slots: InventorySlot[]; equipped: EquippedArmor } | null
```
- `worn = equipped[armorSlot]`; return `null` if none.
- `freeIndex = slots.findIndex(s => s.id === null && s.count === 0)`; **return `null` when the inventory is full** so nothing is destroyed (the command then no-ops, leaving it worn).
- Clone both; `nextSlots[freeIndex] = { ...worn }`; `nextEquipped[armorSlot] = null`.

**`equippedDefense` (line 294)** — drop the `slots` param, read the record:
```
export function equippedDefense(equipped: EquippedArmor): number
```
For each `armorSlot`: `const piece = equipped[armorSlot]`; skip if falsy / wrong `kind`/`armorSlot` / `count<=0`; `defense += (piece.defense ?? 0) + protectionDefense(piece)`. Worn instances carry `defense`/`armorSlot` (from `createSlot`'s `...def` spread), so no `ITEM_DEF_BY_ID` lookup is needed.

**`armorReduction` (line 309)** — drop `slots`:
```
export function armorReduction(equipped): number  // Math.min(0.75, equippedDefense(equipped) * 0.05)
```

**`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (rewrite, line 103)** — operate on and return the record:
```
export function consumeEquippedArmorDurability(equipped, amount = 1, rng?): EquippedArmor | null
```
- Clone the record. For each worn `piece` with `maxDurability`: `rng && unbreakingSkips(piece, rng)` → skip; compute `nextDurability`; if `<= 0` set `next[armorSlot] = null` (broke → destroyed, matching old "slot emptied"); else `next[armorSlot] = { ...piece, durability: nextDurability }`. Return `next` if anything changed, else `null`. **Each mutated piece is cloned**, preserving the immutability contract for the snapshot.

**Remove `unequipMissingArmor` (lines 279–291)** — armor can no longer "leave" the inventory, so there is nothing to reconcile.

Imports stay (`ARMOR_SLOTS`, `createEmptySlot`, `cloneSlots`, `protectionDefense`, `unbreakingSkips`).

## 6. Save format v12 — `lib/game/save.ts`

- **New `serializeEquippedArmor(equipped: EquippedArmor): SavedEquippedArmor`** (next to `inventorySlotsSnapshot`, line 189): for each non-empty worn piece emit `{ id, count, durability, enchantments, customName }` (same per-element shape as `inventorySlotsSnapshot`). Skip empty slots so the field is sparse.
- **Rewrite `restoreEquippedArmor` (line 354)** to read per-slot saved instances through the existing private `restoreSlot` (line 227), which already validates durability/enchantments/customName:
  ```
  export function restoreEquippedArmor(save: SaveData): EquippedArmor | null {
    if (!save.equippedArmor) return null;
    const next = createEmptyArmorEquipment();
    for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {
      const saved = save.equippedArmor[armorSlot];
      if (!saved) continue;
      const slot = restoreSlot(saved);
      if (slot.kind !== "armor" || slot.armorSlot !== armorSlot || slot.count <= 0) continue;
      next[armorSlot] = slot;
    }
    return next;
  }
  ```
  (A saved-broken piece — `durability <= 0` — yields an empty slot from `restoreSlot` and is dropped, matching today's behaviour.)
- **`migrateSaveV11toV12` (recommended: full transform)** — for each legacy `equippedArmor[slot]` id, find and REMOVE the first matching item from `inventorySlots`, moving the whole `SavedSlot` into the armor record (so durability/enchantments/customName survive):
  ```
  export function migrateSaveV11toV12(save: SaveDataV11): SaveData {
    const legacy = save.equippedArmor;                       // SavedArmorById
    if (!legacy || !Array.isArray(save.inventorySlots)) {
      return { ...save, version: 12, equippedArmor: undefined };  // nothing to move
    }
    const slots = save.inventorySlots.slice();               // SavedSlot[]
    const equipped: SavedEquippedArmor = {};
    for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {
      const id = legacy[armorSlot];
      if (!id) continue;
      const def = ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[id];
      if (def?.kind !== "armor" || def.armorSlot !== armorSlot) continue; // drop bad equips
      const idx = slots.findIndex((s) => s?.id === id && s.count > 0);
      if (idx < 0) continue;                                  // item not found → drop the equip
      equipped[armorSlot] = slots[idx];                       // preserves durability/enchants/customName
      slots[idx] = { id: null, count: 0 };
    }
    return { ...save, version: 12, inventorySlots: slots, equippedArmor: equipped };
  }
  ```
- **`readSave` chain (lines 167–179):** add `SaveDataV11` to the `parsed`/`migrated` unions, add `if (migrated.version === 11) migrated = migrateSaveV11toV12(migrated);`, and change the final guard to `if (migrated.version !== 12) return null;`.
- **`writeSave`** unchanged (serializes whatever `serialize()` produced).

**Recommendation:** use the full transform above. The **simpler fallback** (`{ ...save, version: 12, equippedArmor: undefined }` — leave the armor record empty, items stay in the inventory) is data-safe but un-equips everyone's armor on upgrade. The full transform is a pure, well-bounded data rewrite with a built-in drop path, so it is low-risk and preserves the player's loadout. Note that the **legacy `inventoryCounts`-only path** (very old saves without an `inventorySlots` array) hits the early-return branch and therefore behaves exactly like the simple fallback: the equip map is dropped and the armor items remain as ordinary inventory items — acceptable and consistent.

## 8. Edge cases (investigated)

**(a) Death / respawn — safe, no change needed.** `respawn()` (`GameEngine.ts:872`) clears effects/mining/spears/fishing but **does not touch `state.inventory`**, and `applyDamageWithArmor`/`tickRespawnTimer` (`playerLife.ts`) never drop inventory. So the player keeps their inventory across death today; with the fix they also keep the worn-armor record. Behaviour is identical (the worn piece used to ride in inventory, now it rides in the record) — armor survives death consistently with the rest of the loadout. Hardcore game-over (`triggerGameOver`, spectator dead world) still serializes `equippedArmor` fine.

**(b) Unequip with a full inventory** — `unequipArmor` returns `null`, the command no-ops, the piece stays worn. Nothing is destroyed. (Equip-while-full is never a problem: it swaps into the vacated grid index.)

**(c) Snapshot immutability** — the snapshot shares the record reference (`equippedArmor: state.equippedArmor`), exactly as it shares `inventory: state.inventory`. The contract is upheld by the mutators, all of which return fresh records and clone any mutated `InventorySlot`: `toggleEquipArmor`/`unequipArmor` (`{ ...equipped }` + cloned moved slots), `consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (`{ ...equipped }` + `{ ...piece }`), and `mendXp` (`{ ...equipped }` + cloned repaired slot). Verify no code path mutates a worn `InventorySlot` in place. This matches the existing inventory discipline and needs no deep clone in `buildSnapshot`.

**(d) Creative/Spectator / inventory resets** — `switchGameMode` (`GameEngine.ts:803`) does NOT clear inventory or armor; `creativeGiveItem` only adds. `loadNow`/`resetNow` rebuild a whole new engine (armor reinit from save or empty). No special handling required.

- `components/game/InventoryPanel.test.tsx` — the "clicking an armor item equips" (lines 123–131) stays via `onToggleEquipArmor`; the "equipped armor shown / unequips on click" test (lines 133–142) now passes `equippedArmor: { ...createEmptyArmorEquipment(), helmet: createSlot("helmet",1) }` and asserts `onUnequipArmor("helmet")`; add `onUnequipArmor: mock()` to the default props (line 38).
- `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.test.ts` and `systems/fishing.test.ts` — build fake `GameState` with `createEmptyArmorEquipment()` (still all-null, valid); update any assertion that inspects `mendXp`'s return shape.

**Docs:**
- `docs/save-format.md` — change "Schema … `SaveData` (version 11)" (line 5) to 12; add a **v12** bullet to the version history (line ~39) describing dedicated armor storage (`equippedArmor` now persists per-slot `SavedSlot` instances via the shared `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path; `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the record; WORLDGEN_VERSION stays 8, SAVE_KEY unchanged); update the readSave chain text (line 52) to "… → v11 → v12".
- `docs/manual.md` (lines 211–212) and `docs/reference.md` (lines 369–374) — clarify that equipping **moves** the piece from the inventory into its dedicated armor slot (it no longer occupies a hotbar/storage slot).
- `docs/architecture.md` (line 109) — note `inventory.ts` armor functions now read/wear/repair the worn instances in `state.equippedArmor` rather than re-finding them by id in the inventory.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased → Added/Fixed) — entry for the armor-slot fix and the **v8/v9/v10/v11 → v12** bump.

---

## Risks and how to avoid them
- **`EquippedArmor` type ripple into save shapes (highest risk).** If you don't decouple the saved shape, retyping `EquippedArmor` silently corrupts `SaveDataV1..V11.equippedArmor`. Mitigation: the dedicated `SavedArmorById` (legacy) and `SavedEquippedArmor` (v12) types in section 1, and retyping `SaveDataV1.equippedArmor`. TypeScript strict will surface every remaining mismatch.
- **Migration correctness.** Keep the migration a pure transform over `SavedSlot[]` (not runtime slots), remove the moved item by index, and fall back to dropping unmatched/invalid equips. Cover the inventoryCounts-only path (drops the equip map), duplicate-id pieces, and saved-broken pieces in tests.
- **Snapshot shared-mutation.** A single in-place mutation of a worn `InventorySlot` would make a stale snapshot mutate or skip a React render. Mitigation: all four mutators clone (section 8c); grep for any `equippedArmor[...]. = ` style writes outside those functions.
- **Death handling assumption.** Confirmed inventory is kept on death; if a future change adds death-drops it must treat the armor record like inventory. Add a respawn-keeps-armor regression test now to lock the behaviour.
- **Dangling `slots` args.** `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` change arity; the compiler will flag the call sites (`playerLife.ts:17`, `GameEngine.ts:991`, `xp.ts` via `mendXp`, and the tests).

- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/inventory.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/save.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/types.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx
```

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Fix: equipped armor occupies a hotbar/inventory slot → dedicated armor storage (save v12)

## Context

A player reported that equipped armor "takes the space of the hotbar." Diagnosed:
armor is equipped **by reference** — `toggleEquipArmor` only sets
`equippedArmor[slot] = item.id` and leaves the actual item in its inventory slot
(`lib/game/inventory.ts:269`). So a worn helmet that lives in a hotbar slot keeps
occupying it, and renders **twice** (hotbar/grid + armor column). Every armor seam
re-locates the piece with `slots.find(s => s.id === equippedId)`, which is also
ambiguous when two identical pieces exist (the by-id issue CodeRabbit flagged on
#35). This is **pre-existing** (since the inventory module was extracted on
2026-06-11), untouched by the anvil/grindstone/mending work. The docs even claim
"each piece occupies its own equip slot," which the code never implemented.

**Fix:** give armor **dedicated storage** — equipping *moves* the piece out of the
inventory into its armor slot (freeing the hotbar/inventory slot, ending the
double-render); all seams read/wear/repair the worn instances directly. This is the
Minecraft model, matches the docs, and removes the by-id ambiguity.

**Decisions (confirmed with the user):** dedicated armor slots (not a visual-only
patch); land it on a **new branch off `main` AFTER PR #35 merges** — so this builds
on save **v11** + the `customName`/`mendXp` code and bumps the save to **v12**.
Not part of #35.

## Target model

Change `EquippedArmor` from a by-id map to the worn instances:
`Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`. Equip moves the item from inventory into
the record (swapping any worn piece back into the vacated index); unequip moves it
back to the first free inventory slot (no-op if the inventory is full, so nothing is
lost). Worldgen untouched (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8; `SAVE_KEY` unchanged).

## Implementation

### 1. Types + model — `lib/game/types.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`
- `EquippedArmor = Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>` (the runtime type now
  means instances).
- **Decouple the saved shape from the runtime type** (critical — `SaveDataV1.equippedArmor`
  is `Partial<EquippedArmor>` and is inherited by every later `SaveDataVx` via `Omit`):
  - `SavedArmorById = Partial<Record<ArmorSlot, string | null>>` (legacy v1–v11).
  - `SavedEquippedArmor = Partial<Record<ArmorSlot, SavedSlot>>` (v12+; reuses
    `SavedSlot`, which already carries durability/enchantments/customName).
  - Retype `SaveDataV1.equippedArmor?: SavedArmorById`.
  - Add `SaveDataV11 = Omit<SaveDataV10,"version"> & { version: 11 }` and redefine
    `SaveData = Omit<SaveDataV11,"version"|"equippedArmor"> & { version: 12; equippedArmor?: SavedEquippedArmor }`.
- `createEmptyArmorEquipment()` stays all-`null` (valid for the new type; only its
  return type changes).

### 2. Inventory seams — `lib/game/inventory.ts`
- `toggleEquipArmor(slots, equipped, index)` → **moves** the piece; returns
  `{ slots, equipped } | null`. Vacate `slots[index]` (empty, or the previously-worn
  piece → swap), set `equipped[armorSlot] = { ...slot, count: 1 }`. Clone both.
- **New** `unequipArmor(slots, equipped, armorSlot)` → `{ slots, equipped } | null`;
  moves the worn piece to the first empty inventory slot; **returns `null` (no-op)
  when the inventory is full**.
- `equippedDefense(equipped)` and `armorReduction(equipped)` → drop the `slots` param,
  read instances from the record (`piece.defense + protectionDefense(piece)`).
- `consumeEquippedArmorDurability(equipped, amount, rng)` → wears the worn instances,
  cloning each mutated piece; on break sets `equipped[slot] = null`; returns
  `EquippedArmor | null`.
- **Delete** `unequipMissingArmor` (armor can no longer dangle).

### 3. Mending — `lib/game/enchantments.ts`, `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts`
- `mendXp(slots, selectedSlot, equipped, xp)` → `{ slots, equipped, xpLeft }`. Repair
  the held `slots[selectedSlot]` then each worn instance in `equipped` (clone-on-write
  for both; same-ref when nothing repaired). The held/armor dedup dance is gone (the
  two stores are now disjoint). Factor the per-item repair into a small helper.
- `awardXp` wires back both: `state.inventory`/`state.equippedArmor` from the result.

### 4. Damage seam — `lib/game/engine/systems/playerLife.ts:16-17`
- `state.equippedArmor = consumeEquippedArmorDurability(state.equippedArmor, 1, rng) ?? state.equippedArmor;`
  then `armorReduction(state.equippedArmor)`.

### 5. Engine — `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`, `commands.ts`
- `toggleEquipArmor` command writes both stores; **new `unequipArmor {slot}` command**
  (add `ArmorSlot` to the `commands.ts` union).
- Remove `syncEquippedArmor()` (calls at ~591, ~686 and the method ~902-906) — no more
  dangling references to reconcile.
- `serialize()` → `version: 12`, `equippedArmor: serializeEquippedArmor(state.equippedArmor)`.
- Snapshot keeps `equippedArmor: state.equippedArmor` (shares ref like `inventory`;
  correctness from the cloning mutators). `armorPoints: equippedDefense(state.equippedArmor)`.

### 6. Save v12 — `lib/game/save.ts`
- `serializeEquippedArmor(equipped)` → sparse `SavedEquippedArmor` (per-slot
  `{ id, count, durability, enchantments, customName }`, mirroring `inventorySlotsSnapshot`).
- Rewrite `restoreEquippedArmor` to rebuild instances via the existing `restoreSlot`
  (validates kind/slot/durability/enchant/customName; broken pieces drop).
- `migrateSaveV11toV12` (**full transform, recommended**): for each legacy
  `equippedArmor[slot]` id, find+remove the first matching `inventorySlots` item and
  move the whole `SavedSlot` into the record (preserving durability/enchant/customName);
  drop equips whose item/def is invalid or absent. The legacy `inventoryCounts`-only
  path (no `inventorySlots`) falls back to dropping the equip map (items remain as
  ordinary inventory) — acceptable.
- Chain it in `readSave` (extend parse/migrate unions with `SaveDataV11`, add the v11→v12
  step, final guard `!== 12`).

### 7. UI — `InventoryPanel.tsx`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `MinecraftGame.tsx`
- Armor column renders `equippedArmor[armorSlot]` **instances directly** (drop the
  `inventory.findIndex` lookup); clicking a filled armor slot calls a new
  `onUnequipArmor(armorSlot)`. Clicking an armor item in the grid keeps calling
  `onToggleEquipArmor(index)` (now equips-by-move).
- Remove the now-dead `isEquipped` highlight (a worn piece is never in the grid).
- `Hotbar.tsx` needs no change — `inventory.slice(0, hotbarSlots)` no longer contains
  worn pieces, so the slot is genuinely free.
- Thread `unequipArmor` through the hook (`engine.dispatch({type:"unequipArmor",slot})`)
  and `MinecraftGame`.

### Edge cases (validated)
- **Death/respawn**: `respawn()` does not touch `state.inventory`; armor (now in the
  record) survives death exactly as inventory does. Add a regression test locking this.
- **Unequip when full**: no-op, piece stays worn (nothing destroyed).
- **Snapshot immutability**: all four mutators return fresh records + cloned pieces;
  no in-place writes to worn slots.
- **Creative/mode switches**: don't clear inventory/armor; reset/load rebuild the engine.

## Tests
- `inventory.test.ts` — new `toggleEquipArmor` (moves + swap), `unequipArmor` (incl.
  full-inventory refusal), record-based `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/
  `consumeEquippedArmorDurability`; remove the `unequipMissingArmor` test.
- `enchantments.test.ts` — `mendXp` new `{slots,equipped,xpLeft}` shape (armor repair
  reads `result.equipped[slot]`); record-based defense calls.
- `save.test.ts` — `version: 12` sample; **`migrateSaveV11toV12`** (move equip out of
  inventory; drop-when-absent; inventoryCounts fallback); chained-migration version
  assertions → 12; "unknown future version" → 13; armor round-trip preserves
  durability/enchant/customName.
- `GameEngine.test.ts` — build armor item + dispatch `toggleEquipArmor` (no by-id
  set); equip frees the grid slot; `unequipArmor` dispatch; equip→serialize→reload
  round-trip; armor durability via the record; respawn-keeps-armor.
- `InventoryPanel.test.tsx` — armor column renders the instance + `onUnequipArmor`
  fires; equip removes the item from the hotbar (no double-render); add `onUnequipArmor`
  to default props.
- `xp.test.ts` / `fishing.test.ts` — fake state uses `createEmptyArmorEquipment()`
  (still all-null) and the new `mendXp` return.

## Docs
- `docs/save-format.md` — schema → v12; add a v12 history bullet (dedicated armor
  storage via per-slot `SavedSlot`; `migrateSaveV11toV12`; WORLDGEN_VERSION 8, SAVE_KEY
  unchanged); readSave chain "… → v11 → v12".
- `docs/manual.md` + `docs/reference.md` — equipping **moves** the piece into its
  dedicated slot (no longer occupies a hotbar/storage slot).
- `docs/architecture.md` — armor seams now read/wear/repair `state.equippedArmor`
  instances, not re-found-by-id inventory items.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — armor-slot fix + save v11→v12 bump.

## Verification
1. `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run format:check && bun test && bun run build`
   (the changed seam arities make `tsc` flag every call site — a feature here).
2. `bun run test:e2e` (touches inventory UI + save) — note the save-version assertion
   in `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts` becomes 12.
3. Manual (`bun run dev`): put a helmet in a hotbar slot → equip it → the hotbar slot
   becomes empty and usable, the helmet shows only in the armor column; unequip →
   returns to a free slot; with a full inventory, unequip is refused; take damage to
   confirm defense + durability wear; Mending repairs worn armor; save + reload keeps
   the worn loadout; an older (v11) world migrates with armor still equipped.

When `rng` is supplied, each piece's Unbreaking\n * enchant may skip its wear. Returns a new record, or null when nothing changed.\n */\nexport function consumeEquippedArmorDurability(equipped: EquippedArmor, amount = 1, rng?: () => number): EquippedArmor | null {\n  if (amount <= 0) return null;\n  const next = { ...equipped };\n  let changed = false;\n  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {\n    const piece = next[armorSlot];\n    if (!piece?.maxDurability) continue;\n    if (rng && unbreakingSkips(piece, rng)) continue; // this piece's Unbreaking saved its wear\n    const nextDurability = (piece.durability ?? piece.maxDurability) - amount;\n    next[armorSlot] = nextDurability <= 0 ? null : { ...piece, durability: nextDurability };\n    changed = true;\n  }\n  return changed ? next : null;\n}"

85	/**
86	 * Mending seam: diverts gained XP to repair the player's damaged, Mending-enchanted
87	 * gear — the held item first, then equipped armor in ARMOR_SLOTS order — at
88	 * MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP durability per diverted XP point. Returns a new slots array
89	 * (same ref when nothing was repaired) plus the XP left to bank. The one reader for
90	 * Mending: `awardXp` is its only caller.
91	 */
92	export function mendXp(slots: InventorySlot[], selectedSlot: number, equipped: EquippedArmor, xp: number): { slots: InventorySlot[]; xpLeft: number } {
93	  if (xp <= 0) return { slots, xpLeft: xp };
94	
95	  // Held item first, then each equipped armor piece (skipping a held piece already listed).
96	  const indices: number[] = [];
97	  if (selectedSlot >= 0 && selectedSlot < slots.length) indices.push(selectedSlot);
98	  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {
99	    const id = equipped[armorSlot];
100	    if (!id) continue;
101	    const i = slots.findIndex((s) => s.id === id && s.count > 0);
102	    if (i >= 0 && !indices.includes(i)) indices.push(i);
103	  }
104	
105	  let remaining = xp;
106	  let next = slots;
107	  for (const i of indices) {
108	    if (remaining <= 0) break;
109	    const slot = next[i];
110	    if (!slot?.maxDurability || enchantLevel(slot, "mending") <= 0) continue;
111	    const missing = slot.maxDurability - (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability);
112	    if (missing <= 0) continue;
113	    const xpNeeded = Math.ceil(missing / MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);
114	    const xpUsed = Math.min(remaining, xpNeeded);
115	    const repaired = Math.min(missing, xpUsed * MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);
116	    if (next === slots) next = slots.slice(); // clone on first write
117	    next[i] = { ...slot, durability: (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability) + repaired };
118	    remaining -= xpUsed;
119	  }
120	  return { slots: next, xpLeft: remaining };
121	}

The one reader for\n * Mending: `awardXp` is its only caller.\n */\nexport function mendXp(slots: InventorySlot[], selectedSlot: number, equipped: EquippedArmor, xp: number): { slots: InventorySlot[]; xpLeft: number } {\n  if (xp <= 0) return { slots, xpLeft: xp };\n\n  // Held item first, then each equipped armor piece (skipping a held piece already listed).\n  const indices: number[] = [];\n  if (selectedSlot >= 0 && selectedSlot < slots.length) indices.push(selectedSlot);\n  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {\n    const id = equipped[armorSlot];\n    if (!id) continue;\n    const i = slots.findIndex((s) => s.id === id && s.count > 0);\n    if (i >= 0 && !indices.includes(i)) indices.push(i);\n  }\n\n  let remaining = xp;\n  let next = slots;\n  for (const i of indices) {\n    if (remaining <= 0) break;\n    const slot = next[i];\n    if (!slot?.maxDurability || enchantLevel(slot, \"mending\") <= 0) continue;\n    const missing = slot.maxDurability - (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability);\n    if (missing <= 0) continue;\n    const xpNeeded = Math.ceil(missing / MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);\n    const xpUsed = Math.min(remaining, xpNeeded);\n    const repaired = Math.min(missing, xpUsed * MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);\n    if (next === slots) next = slots.slice(); // clone on first write\n    next[i] = { ...slot, durability: (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability) + repaired };\n    remaining -= xpUsed;\n  }\n  return { slots: next, xpLeft: remaining };\n}",
  "new_string": "/** Repairs one Mending slot with up to `xp` points; returns the repaired slot + XP used, or null when there's nothing to do. */\nfunction repairWithXp(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined, xp: number): { slot: InventorySlot; xpUsed: number } | null {\n  if (!slot?.maxDurability || enchantLevel(slot, \"mending\") <= 0) return null;\n  const missing = slot.maxDurability - (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability);\n  if (missing <= 0) return null;\n  const xpNeeded = Math.ceil(missing / MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);\n  const xpUsed = Math.min(xp, xpNeeded);\n  const repaired = Math.min(missing, xpUsed * MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP);\n  return { slot: { ...slot, durability: (slot.durability ?? slot.maxDurability) + repaired }, xpUsed };\n}\n\n/**\n * Mending seam: diverts gained XP to repair the player's damaged, Mending-enchanted\n * gear — the held item first, then worn armor in ARMOR_SLOTS order — at\n * MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP durability per diverted XP point. Returns (possibly new)\n * slots + equipped records (same refs when nothing was repaired) plus the XP left\n * to bank. The one reader for Mending: `awardXp` is its only caller.\n */\nexport function mendXp(\n  slots: InventorySlot[],\n  selectedSlot: number,\n  equipped: EquippedArmor,\n  xp: number\n): { slots: InventorySlot[]; equipped: EquippedArmor; xpLeft: number } {\n  if (xp <= 0) return { slots, equipped, xpLeft: xp };\n  let remaining = xp;\n  let nextSlots = slots;\n  let nextEquipped = equipped;\n\n  // Held item first (worn armor lives in `equipped`, a disjoint store).\n  if (remaining > 0 && selectedSlot >= 0 && selectedSlot < slots.length) {\n    const r = repairWithXp(slots[selectedSlot], remaining);\n    if (r) {\n      nextSlots = slots.slice();\n      nextSlots[selectedSlot] = r.slot;\n      remaining -= r.xpUsed;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Then each worn armor piece.\n  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {\n    if (remaining <= 0) break;\n    const r = repairWithXp(nextEquipped[armorSlot], remaining);\n    if (!r) continue;\n    if (nextEquipped === equipped) nextEquipped = { ...equipped }; // clone on first write\n    nextEquipped[armorSlot] = r.slot;\n    remaining -= r.xpUsed;\n  }\n\n  return { slots: nextSlots, equipped: nextEquipped, xpLeft: remaining };\n}"
}

6	/**
7	 * Applies armor-mitigated damage (always at least 1) and wears equipped armor.
8	 * Returns true when the hit was lethal — the engine emits the death event.
9	 * Creative/Spectator are invulnerable, so every damage source no-ops here.
10	 */
11	export function applyDamageWithArmor(state: GameState, amount: number, rng?: () => number): boolean {
12	  if (state.isDead || !takesDamage(state.gameMode)) return false;
13	  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
14	  if (value <= 0) return false;
15	
16	  state.inventory = consumeEquippedArmorDurability(state.inventory, state.equippedArmor, 1, rng) ?? state.inventory;
17	  const reduction = armorReduction(state.inventory, state.equippedArmor);
18	  const mitigated = Math.max(1, Math.floor(value * (1 - reduction)));
19	
20	  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - mitigated);
21	  if (state.hearts > 0) return false;
22	
23	  state.isDead = true;
24	  state.respawnTimer = RESPAWN_SECONDS;
25	  return true;
26	}
27

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/save.ts",
  "old_string": "export function migrateSaveV10toV11(save: SaveDataV10): SaveData {\n  return { ...save, version: 11 };\n}\n\n// Storage is injectable so save logic can be tested without a browser.",
  "new_string": "export function migrateSaveV10toV11(save: SaveDataV10): SaveDataV11 {\n  return { ...save, version: 11 };\n}\n\n/**\n * Migrates a v11 save to v12 — armor moves to dedicated storage. The legacy\n * `equippedArmor` was a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` (the worn item also\n * lived in the inventory). For each valid equip, move the matching inventory item\n * out into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName); drop\n * equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor for the slot. Pre-`inventorySlots`\n * (legacy counts-only) saves simply drop the equip map and keep items in inventory.\n */\nexport function migrateSaveV11toV12(save: SaveDataV11): SaveData {\n  const legacy = save.equippedArmor;\n  if (!legacy || !Array.isArray(save.inventorySlots)) {\n    return { ...save, version: 12, equippedArmor: undefined };\n  }\n  const slots = save.inventorySlots.slice();\n  const equipped: SavedEquippedArmor = {};\n  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {\n    const id = legacy[armorSlot];\n    if (!id) continue;\n    const def = ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[id];\n    if (def?.kind !== \"armor\" || def.armorSlot !== armorSlot) continue; // drop invalid equips\n    const idx = slots.findIndex((s) => s?.id === id && s.count > 0);\n    if (idx < 0) continue; // item not in inventory → drop the equip\n    equipped[armorSlot] = slots[idx]; // preserves durability/enchantments/customName\n    slots[idx] = { id: null, count: 0 };\n  }\n  return { ...save, version: 12, inventorySlots: slots, equippedArmor: equipped };\n}\n\n// Storage is injectable so save logic can be tested without a browser."
}

  "new_string": "/** Restores worn armor, rebuilding each piece through restoreSlot and dropping anything that isn't valid armor for its slot. */\nexport function restoreEquippedArmor(save: SaveData): EquippedArmor | null {\n  if (!save.equippedArmor) return null;\n  const next = createEmptyArmorEquipment();\n  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {\n    const saved = save.equippedArmor[armorSlot];\n    if (!saved) continue;\n    const slot = restoreSlot(saved);\n    if (slot.kind !== \"armor\" || slot.armorSlot !== armorSlot || slot.count <= 0) continue;\n    next[armorSlot] = slot;\n  }\n  return next;\n}"
}

// nothing worn\n    const full = Array.from({ length: INVENTORY_SLOTS }, () => createSlot(\"dirt\", 1));\n    expect(unequipArmor(full, equipped, \"helmet\")).toBeNull(); // inventory full → no-op\n  });\n\n  test(\"armorReduction is 5% per defense point and capped\", () => {\n    const equipped = { ...createEmptyArmorEquipment(), helmet: createSlot(\"helmet\", 1), chestplate: createSlot(\"chestplate\", 1) };\n    expect(armorReduction(equipped)).toBeCloseTo((2 + 4) * 0.05);\n    expect(armorReduction(createEmptyArmorEquipment())).toBe(0);\n  });\n\n  test(\"equippedDefense sums defense points of worn pieces\", () => {\n    const equipped = { ...createEmptyArmorEquipment(), helmet: createSlot(\"helmet\", 1), chestplate: createSlot(\"chestplate\", 1) };\n    expect(equippedDefense(equipped)).toBe(2 + 4);\n    expect(equippedDefense(createEmptyArmorEquipment())).toBe(0);\n  });\n});"

54	    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
55	    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
56	  };
57	}
58	
59	function makeEngine(save: ReturnType<GameEngine["serialize"]> | null = null): GameEngine {
60	  return new GameEngine({ save, seed: 1337, rng: mulberry32(42), worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } });
61	}

5	`SaveData` (version 11) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
6	
7	- world `seed`
8	- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
9	- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
10	- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
11	- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
12	- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
13	- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
14	- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
15	- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
16	- equipped armor
```

37:### Version history
39:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
40:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
```

53:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11.

48:5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
58:**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
109:- `inventory.ts` — pure slot algebra (`adjustSlotCount`, `craft`, durability, armor); every function returns a new array or `null` for "no change". Crafting refuses when the result doesn't fit rather than destroying overflow.
110:- `items.ts` — `ITEM_DEFS`, `BLOCK_TO_SLOT`, `BREAK_HARDNESS`, armor slots, slot factories. `recipes.ts` — `RECIPES` (each with an optional `station`, e.g. `"furnace"` for smelting).
138:- **Being in water is not "stuck"**: the unstuck teleport fires only on solid-block overlap or falling below the world (y < 2). Don't make water count as a collision in `collidesAt` — players may stay submerged, though `tickWaterExposure` starts armor-bypassing damage after 60 continuous seconds. Its transient timers reset on exit and are never serialized.

Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change
10	- **Anvil**: a new crafted station (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**) for maintaining and consolidating gear, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted dark-iron block, reusing existing synth for its clang). The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
11	  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels. Three actions: **Combine** a duplicate (adds the two durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate); **Repair** with the item's tier material (e.g. diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble for a stone pickaxe) for a chunk of durability without a second copy; and **Rename** (the custom name shows everywhere the item's label does)
12	  - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. The anvil station id is threaded through the **engine/UI** `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`); the panel is a new `AnvilColumn`. A per-item `customName` (additive v11 field, durable gear only, trimmed + capped) persists the rename, surfaced everywhere via a shared `displayName` helper

Equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (swapping any worn piece back into the freed index); unequipping moves it back to the first free slot, and is **refused when the inventory is full** so nothing is lost. The defense, durability, and Mending seams read/wear/repair those instances directly — no more find-by-id, so the duplicate-piece ambiguity disappears too. `syncEquippedArmor`/`unequipMissingArmor` are removed (armor can no longer dangle).\n\nBecause the `EquippedArmor` type ripples through the combat/durability/Mending seams, the engine, the save, and the inventory UI, this lands as **one atomic commit** rather than separately-green slices.\n\n## Save format v11 → v12\n\n`equippedArmor` persists as per-slot `SavedSlot` (preserving worn durability/enchantments/customName) via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`. `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record, dropping equips whose item is missing or invalid. No worldgen change (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8); `SAVE_KEY` unchanged. ## Investigation Report: Armor Rendering in Third-Person Player Model

Based on a thorough code exploration, here are my findings:

---

## 1. Third-Person Player Model Construction

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`

The third-person player body is built as a simple humanoid using Three.js Box geometries with pivot groups at joints:

**Key construction code (lines 35–128):**
```typescript
export function createPlayerModel(palette: PlayerPalette = DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE): PlayerModel {
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  // ...
  
  // Legs: hip pivots at y=0.72, meshes hanging below (pants + shoe band).
  const makeLeg = (x: number) => {
    const pivot = new THREE.Group();
    pivot.position.set(x, 0.72, 0);
    const leg = box(0.2, 0.6, 0.2, pantsMat);
    leg.position.y = -0.36;
    const shoe = box(0.21, 0.12, 0.22, shoeMat);
    shoe.position.set(0, -0.66, 0.005);
    pivot.add(leg, shoe);
    group.add(pivot);
    return pivot;
  };
  
  // Torso: single box spanning y 0.72–1.32
  const torso = box(0.46, 0.6, 0.24, shirtMat);
  torso.position.y = 1.02;
  group.add(torso);
  
  // Arms: shoulder pivots just below torso top
  const makeArm = (x: number) => {
    const pivot = new THREE.Group();
    pivot.position.set(x, 1.26, 0);
    const arm = box(0.16, 0.66, 0.16, skinMat);
    arm.position.y = -0.33;
    pivot.add(arm);
    group.add(pivot);
    return pivot;
  };
  
  // Head: neck pivot at y=1.32 with skull, hair, eyes
  const head = new THREE.Group();
  head.position.set(0, 1.32, 0);
  const skull = box(0.4, 0.4, 0.4, skinMat);
  // ... eyes, hair added to head
  group.add(head);
  
  return { group, head, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg, itemHolder, paletteMaterials, materials, geometries };
}
```

**Structure:**
- **Root:** `group` (THREE.Group) — all body parts attached
- **Limbs:** `leftLeg`, `rightLeg`, `leftArm`, `rightArm` — pivot groups (THREE.Group) at joints, containing box meshes
- **Head:** Separate pivot group with skull mesh, hair, and eyes
- **Item holder:** Anchored to right arm for held items
- **Materials:** One per palette slot (skin, hair, shirt, pants, shoes, eyeWhite, eyePupil) — all named and tracked in `paletteMaterials` Record

---

## 2. Does It Render Armor? **NO — Definitively No**

**Search Results:** 
- Zero references to `equippedArmor` anywhere in `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/` (all files searched)
- Only one hit for "armor" in render code: a comment in `itemModel.ts` line 30 about how *items* (including armor as inventory items) are rendered, not body armor
- `PlayerVisualsState` type (lines 12–27 of `playerVisuals.ts`) does NOT include any armor field
- No armor-related tinting, material swaps, or mesh toggling in any render file

**Verdict:** Armor visuals on the third-person player model **were never implemented**. This is not a regression—it's an unimplemented feature. The player can equip and wear armor (tracked by the engine, provides defense), but the renderer never draws it on the body.

---

## 3. How Armor Data Reaches the Renderer (or Doesn't)

**Call chain:**
1. `GameRenderer.sync(state: GameState, timeMs)` — line 184 of `GameRenderer.ts` receives full `GameState` which contains `equippedArmor: EquippedArmor` (line 152 of `state.ts`)
2. Calls `this.playerVisuals.sync(state, timeMs)` — line 210 of `GameRenderer.ts`
3. `playerVisuals.sync(state: PlayerVisualsState, timeMs)` — line 31 of `playerVisuals.ts`

**Problem:** The `PlayerVisualsState` type (lines 12–27 of `playerVisuals.ts`) is:
```typescript
export type PlayerVisualsState = {
  cameraMode: CameraMode;
  gameMode: GameMode;
  isDead: boolean;
  player: { position, velocity, yaw, pitch, onGround };
  inventory: InventorySlot[];
  selectedSlot: number;
  mining: { targetKey: string };
  fishing: FishingState | null;
};
```

**Note:** Despite `GameState` being passed structurally (TypeScript duck-typing), the `sync()` function body only reads the fields in `PlayerVisualsState`. It never accesses `equippedArmor` from the state. The armor data is *available* in the state but *completely ignored* by the sync logic (lines 82–131 of `playerVisuals.ts`).

---

## 4. Camera Modes

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/cameraView.ts`

Camera modes: `"first"` | `"third-rear"` | `"third-front"`

**Player visibility logic** (line 84 of `playerVisuals.ts`):
```typescript
const visible = state.cameraMode !== "first" && !state.isDead && state.gameMode !== "spectator";
model.group.visible = visible;
```

The third-person player body **only renders in third-person camera modes** (`"third-rear"` or `"third-front"`). In first-person mode, the body is hidden (as expected). So when the user switches to third-person, they see the bare body—and because armor rendering is unimplemented, no armor appears.

---

## 5. Skin / Per-Part Coloring System

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/playerSkins.ts`

Each player skin is a **palette** with colors for different body parts:
```typescript
export type PlayerPalette = {
  skin: number;      // hex color for face/arms
  hair: number;      // top of head
  shirt: number;     // torso
  pants: number;     // legs
  shoes: number;     // feet
  eyeWhite: number;  // eye whites
  eyePupil: number;  // eye pupils
};
```

**Example palettes** (lines 28–60 of `playerSkins.ts`):
- `"default"` (Steve): `{ skin: 0xc68e63, hair: 0x4a3220, shirt: 0x2e8b83, pants: 0x3b3f8f, shoes: 0x4a3527, ... }`
- `"knight"`: Metallic grays—`{ skin: 0xaab2bd, shirt: 0x8d96a3, ... }`

**How applied:**
1. `createPlayerModel(palette)` creates one `THREE.MeshStandardMaterial` per palette slot (lines 40–60 of `playerModel.ts`)
2. Each material is stored in `paletteMaterials: Record<keyof PlayerPalette, THREE.MeshStandardMaterial>`
3. `applyPalette(model, palette)` updates colors live (lines 28–33 of `playerModel.ts`):
```typescript
export function applyPalette(model: PlayerModel, palette: PlayerPalette): void {
  for (const key of Object.keys(model.paletteMaterials) as Array<keyof PlayerPalette>) {
    model.paletteMaterials[key].color.setHex(palette[key]);
  }
}
```

**Pattern for Armor Overlay:**
The cleanest way to add armor would follow this exact pattern:
- Add `helmet`, `chestplate`, `leggings`, `boots` materials to `paletteMaterials`
- Create slightly larger box meshes as overlay shells over the body parts (legs, torso, head)
- Add them as children to the existing limb pivot groups
- Toggle visibility based on `equippedArmor[slot] !== null`
- Optionally tint by durability percentage

---

## 6. Mob Models for Reference

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/mobModel.ts`

Mob models use the **same part-group construction pattern** as the player:
```typescript
export function createMobModel(
  bodyColor: number, headColor: number, legColor: number, 
  eyeColor: number, detailColor: number,
  bodySize: [w, h, d], headSize: [w, h, d]
): MobModel {
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  const materials = [
    new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: bodyColor, roughness: 0.86, metalness: 0.02 }),
    new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: headColor, ... }),
    new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: legColor, ... }),
    // ... more materials
  ];
  
  const body = new THREE.Mesh(bodyGeo, materials[0]);
  const head = new THREE.Mesh(headGeo, materials[1]);
  const legs: THREE.Mesh[] = []; // 4 leg meshes
  // ... assemble and return
}
```

**Observation:** Mob models also do **not render armor**, despite many mobs (skeletons, zombies) traditionally wearing armor in Minecraft. This confirms the armor visualization feature is globally unimplemented.

---

## 7. Final Verdict

### **Armor Is Completely Unimplemented on the Third-Person Player Model**

**Evidence:**

1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import { DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE, type PlayerPalette } from "@/lib/game/playerSkins";
3	
4	/**
5	 * The player's own body, visible only in third person. Box-mesh humanoid in
6	 * the same zero-asset style as the mobs, but with two arms and pivot groups at
7	 * the shoulders/hips so limbs swing about their joints instead of their
8	 * centers. The group origin sits at the feet and the face is built on the -Z
9	 * side, so `group.rotation.y = player.yaw` matches the camera convention
10	 * (forward at yaw 0 is -Z).
11	 */
12	export type PlayerModel = {
13	  group: THREE.Group;
14	  /** Neck pivot — apply the look pitch here so the body stays upright. */
15	  head: THREE.Group;
16	  leftArm: THREE.Group;
17	  rightArm: THREE.Group;
18	  leftLeg: THREE.Group;
19	  rightLeg: THREE.Group;
20	  /** Hand anchor inside the right arm — the held item model goes here. */
21	  itemHolder: THREE.Group;
22	  /** One material per palette slot, for live recolors; also listed in `materials`. */
23	  paletteMaterials: Record<keyof PlayerPalette, THREE.MeshStandardMaterial>;
24	  materials: THREE.Material[];
25	  geometries: THREE.BufferGeometry[];
26	};
27	
28	/** Recolors an existing model in place — no allocation, safe to call live. */
29	export function applyPalette(model: PlayerModel, palette: PlayerPalette): void {
30	  for (const key of Object.keys(model.paletteMaterials) as Array<keyof PlayerPalette>) {
31	    model.paletteMaterials[key].color.setHex(palette[key]);
32	  }
33	}
34	
35	export function createPlayerModel(palette: PlayerPalette = DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE): PlayerModel {
36	  const group = new THREE.Group();
37	  const materials: THREE.Material[] = [];
38	  const geometries: THREE.BufferGeometry[] = [];
39	
40	  const material = (color: number) => {
41	    const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness: 0.85, metalness: 0.02 });
42	    materials.push(mat);
43	    return mat;
44	  };
45	  const box = (w: number, h: number, d: number, mat: THREE.Material) => {
46	    const geometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d);
47	    geometries.push(geometry);
48	    return new THREE.Mesh(geometry, mat);
49	  };
50	
51	  // `materials` stays the single disposal authority; this record only names them.
52	  const paletteMaterials: PlayerModel["paletteMaterials"] = {
53	    skin: material(palette.skin),
54	    hair: material(palette.hair),
55	    shirt: material(palette.shirt),
56	    pants: material(palette.pants),
57	    shoes: material(palette.shoes),
58	    eyeWhite: material(palette.eyeWhite),
59	    eyePupil: material(palette.eyePupil)
60	  };
61	  const skinMat = paletteMaterials.skin;
62	  const shirtMat = paletteMaterials.shirt;
63	  const pantsMat = paletteMaterials.pants;
64	  const shoeMat = paletteMaterials.shoes;
65	
66	  // Legs: hip pivots at y=0.72, meshes hanging below (pants + shoe band).
67	  const makeLeg = (x: number) => {
68	    const pivot = new THREE.Group();
69	    pivot.position.set(x, 0.72, 0);
70	    const leg = box(0.2, 0.6, 0.2, pantsMat);
71	    leg.position.y = -0.36;
72	    const shoe = box(0.21, 0.12, 0.22, shoeMat);
73	    shoe.position.set(0, -0.66, 0.005);
74	    pivot.add(leg, shoe);
75	    group.add(pivot);
76	    return pivot;
77	  };
78	  const leftLeg = makeLeg(-0.11);
79	  const rightLeg = makeLeg(0.11);
80	
81	  // Torso spans y 0.72–1.32.
82	  const torso = box(0.46, 0.6, 0.24, shirtMat);
83	  torso.position.y = 1.02;
84	  group.add(torso);
85	
86	  // Arms: shoulder pivots just below the torso top; bare skin like Steve.
87	  const makeArm = (x: number) => {
88	    const pivot = new THREE.Group();
89	    pivot.position.set(x, 1.26, 0);
90	    const arm = box(0.16, 0.66, 0.16, skinMat);
91	    arm.position.y = -0.33;
92	    pivot.add(arm);
93	    group.add(pivot);
94	    return pivot;
95	  };
96	  const leftArm = makeArm(-0.31);
97	  const rightArm = makeArm(0.31);
98	  rightArm.name = "rightArm";
99	
100	  // Hand anchor at the end of the right arm, tilted slightly forward so held
101	  // items read as carried rather than glued flat to the limb.
102	  const itemHolder = new THREE.Group();
103	  itemHolder.name = "itemHolder";
104	  itemHolder.position.set(0, -0.62, -0.1);
105	  itemHolder.rotation.x = -0.5;
106	  itemHolder.scale.setScalar(0.8);
107	  rightArm.add(itemHolder);
108	
109	  // Head on a neck pivot; the face (eyes) is on the -Z side.
110	  const head = new THREE.Group();
111	  head.name = "head";
112	  head.position.set(0, 1.32, 0);
113	  const skull = box(0.4, 0.4, 0.4, skinMat);
114	  skull.position.y = 0.23;
115	  const hair = box(0.42, 0.12, 0.42, paletteMaterials.hair);
116	  hair.position.y = 0.4;
117	  head.add(skull, hair);
118	  for (const side of [-1, 1]) {
119	    const white = box(0.09, 0.07, 0.02, paletteMaterials.eyeWhite);
120	    white.position.set(side * 0.09, 0.26, -0.2);
121	    const pupil = box(0.04, 0.07, 0.02, paletteMaterials.eyePupil);
122	    pupil.position.set(side * 0.07, 0.26, -0.205);
123	    head.add(white, pupil);
124	  }
125	  group.add(head);
126	
127	  return { group, head, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg, itemHolder, paletteMaterials, materials, geometries };
128	}
129

11	/** The slice of GameState the player body needs — narrow so tests stay light. */
12	export type PlayerVisualsState = {
13	  cameraMode: CameraMode;
14	  gameMode: GameMode;
15	  isDead: boolean;
16	  player: {
17	    position: THREE.Vector3;
18	    velocity: THREE.Vector3;
19	    yaw: number;
20	    pitch: number;
21	    onGround: boolean;
22	  };
23	  inventory: InventorySlot[];
24	  selectedSlot: number;
25	  mining: { targetKey: string };
26	  fishing: FishingState | null;
27	};
28	
29	export type PlayerVisuals = {
30	  /** Positions, animates, and shows/hides the body. Call once per frame. */
31	  sync(state: PlayerVisualsState, timeMs: number): void;
32	  /** Queues a one-shot arm swing (attack click); latched on the next sync. */
33	  triggerSwing(): void;
34	  /** Queues a one-shot cast flick; latched on the next sync. */
35	  triggerCast(): void;
36	  /** Queues a one-shot reel pull-back; latched on the next sync. */
37	  triggerReel(): void;
38	  /** World position of the third-person rod tip (hand anchor) — for the fishing line origin. */
39	  getRodTip(out: THREE.Vector3): THREE.Vector3;
40	  /** Recolors the body in place (skin preset change) — live-safe. */
41	  setPalette(palette: PlayerPalette): void;
42	  dispose(): void;
43	};
44	
45	export function createPlayerVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): PlayerVisuals {
46	  const model = createPlayerModel();
47	  model.group.visible = false;
48	  scene.add(model.group);
49	
50	  let heldModel: ItemModel | null = null;
51	  let heldKey = "";
52	  let swingQueued = false;
53	  let swingStartMs = -Infinity;
54	  let castQueued = false;
55	  let castStartMs = -Infinity;
56	  let reelQueued = false;
57	  let reelStartMs = -Infinity;
58	  let wasMining = false;
59	
60	  const clearHeldModel = () => {
61	    if (!heldModel) return;
62	    model.itemHolder.remove(heldModel.object);
63	    heldModel.geometry.dispose();
64	    heldModel.material.dispose();
65	    heldModel = null;
66	    heldKey = "";
67	  };
68	
69	  const syncHeldItem = (slot: InventorySlot | undefined) => {
70	    const nextKey = slot?.id && slot.count > 0 && slot.kind ? slot.id : "";
71	    if (nextKey === heldKey) return;
72	    clearHeldModel();
73	    const built = buildItemModel(slot);
74	    if (built) {
75	      heldModel = built;
76	      heldKey = nextKey;
77	      model.itemHolder.add(built.object);
78	    }
79	  };
80	
81	  return {
82	    sync(state, timeMs) {
83	      // Spectator is unseen — the body stays hidden even in third-person.
84	      const visible = state.cameraMode !== "first" && !state.isDead && state.gameMode !== "spectator";
85	      model.group.visible = visible;
86	      if (!visible) {
87	        // Don't replay stale one-shots when the body next becomes visible.
88	        swingQueued = false;
89	        castQueued = false;
90	        reelQueued = false;
91	        return;
92	      }
93	
94	      const { player } = state;
95	      model.group.position.copy(player.position);
96	      model.group.rotation.y = player.yaw;
97	      model.head.rotation.x = player.pitch;
98	
99	      syncHeldItem(state.inventory[state.selectedSlot]);
100	
101	      const miningActive = state.mining.targetKey !== "";
102	      if (swingQueued) {
103	        swingQueued = false;
104	        swingStartMs = timeMs;
105	      }
106	      if (castQueued) {
107	        castQueued = false;
108	        castStartMs = timeMs;
109	      }
110	      if (reelQueued) {
111	        reelQueued = false;
112	        reelStartMs = timeMs;
113	      }
114	      if (miningActive && !wasMining) swingStartMs = timeMs;
115	      wasMining = miningActive;
116	
117	      const moveFactor = player.onGround ? Math.min(1, Math.hypot(player.velocity.x, player.velocity.z) / WALK_SPEED) : 0;
118	      const pose = computePlayerPose({
119	        timeMs,
120	        moveFactor,
121	        miningActive,
122	        swingStartMs,
123	        castStartMs,
124	        reelStartMs,
125	        fishingActive: state.fishing !== null
126	      });
127	      model.leftArm.rotation.x = pose.leftArmX;
128	      model.rightArm.rotation.x = pose.rightArmX;
129	      model.leftLeg.rotation.x = pose.leftLegX;
130	      model.rightLeg.rotation.x = pose.rightLegX;
131	    },
132	
133	    triggerSwing() {
134	      swingQueued = true;
135	    },
136	
137	    triggerCast() {
138	      castQueued = true;
139	    },
140	
141	    triggerReel() {
142	      reelQueued = true;
143	    },
144	
145	    getRodTip(out) {
146	      // Flush the holder's parent chain (group → right arm → holder) so the world
147	      // position is current this frame, not one frame stale. Call after sync().
148	      model.itemHolder.updateWorldMatrix(true, false);
149	      return model.itemHolder.getWorldPosition(out);
150	    },
151	
152	    setPalette(palette) {
153	      applyPalette(model, palette);
154	    },
155	
156	    dispose() {
157	      clearHeldModel();
158	      scene.remove(model.group);
159	      for (const material of model.materials) material.dispose();
160	      for (const geometry of model.geometries) geometry.dispose();
161	    }
162	  };
163	}
164

You're right that there's no armor on the body — and I checked: it's **not a regression**, it's simply **never been implemented**. The third-person player model (`playerModel.ts`) only ever draws the bare body (head/torso/arms/legs); there's zero `equippedArmor` reference anywhere in `lib/game/render/`, and `playerVisuals.sync` never reads what's worn. (Mobs don't render armor either.)

So this is a small **visual feature**: draw procedural armor "shells" (slightly larger tinted boxes, matching the zero-asset voxel style) over the body parts, parented to the same pivots so they animate with the limbs, and toggle each piece's visibility by what's equipped. It's self-contained — `playerModel.ts` (build the shells), `playerVisuals.ts` (`PlayerVisualsState` gains `equippedArmor`, sync toggles them), no engine/save/logic changes. The 6 slots map naturally: helmet→head, face_mask→face visor, neck_protection→neck band, chestplate→torso (+shoulder caps), leggings→upper legs, boots→feet.

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Show equipped armor on the third-person player model

## Context

A player noticed that wearing armor and switching to a third-person camera shows a
**bare body — no armor on it**. Investigation confirms this is **not a regression**:
armor visuals on the player model were never implemented. `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`
builds only bare body parts, `playerVisuals.sync` never reads what's worn, and there
is zero `equippedArmor` reference anywhere in `lib/game/render/`.

**Fix:** draw procedural armor "shell" boxes (slightly larger than each body part, in
the zero-asset voxel style) over the body, parented to the existing pivots so they
animate with the limbs, and toggle each piece's visibility by what's equipped. No
engine/save/logic changes — purely a renderer addition.

**Decisions (confirmed with the user):**
- **Bundle onto the open PR #36** (`fix/armor-dedicated-slots`), so it ships with the
  armor-storage fix. The branch already has the v12 instance model
  (`equippedArmor: Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`), so the renderer reads
  the worn instance directly.
- **Per-slot ore tint** — each piece is colored toward the ore it's crafted from
  (each slot holds one item type, so the tint is a fixed per-slot color).

## Implementation

### 1. `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts` — build the shells

- Extend `PlayerModel` with `armor: Record<ArmorSlot, THREE.Mesh[]>` (the overlay
  shells per slot, so `playerVisuals` can toggle them). Import `ArmorSlot` from
  `@/lib/game/types`.
- In `createPlayerModel`, after the body parts, build one **armor material per slot**
  (`MeshStandardMaterial`, `metalness ≈ 0.6`, `roughness ≈ 0.4`) colored from a
  per-slot ore tint, push each to `materials` (the disposal authority), and create
  shell boxes (each via the existing `box()` helper so geometries land in
  `geometries`). All shells start `visible = false`. Attach each to the pivot that
  owns the body part it covers, so it inherits the limb animation:
  - **helmet** → a crown box (~`0.46×0.30×0.46` at local `y≈0.33`) on the `head` pivot.
  - **face_mask** → a thin front plate (~`0.42×0.22×0.05` at `y≈0.22, z≈-0.21`) on `head`.
  - **neck_protection** → a band (~`0.36×0.12×0.30` at world `y≈1.30`) on the root `group` (static).
  - **chestplate** → torso shell (~`0.52×0.62×0.30` at `y=1.02`) on `group`, plus a
    shoulder cap (~`0.22×0.18×0.22` at local `y≈-0.05`) on each of `leftArm`/`rightArm`
    pivots → `armor.chestplate = [torsoShell, leftShoulder, rightShoulder]`.
  - **leggings** → an upper-leg shell (~`0.24×0.42×0.24` at local `y≈-0.26`) on each
    of `leftLeg`/`rightLeg`.
  - **boots** → a lower-leg/foot shell (~`0.26×0.20×0.28` at local `y≈-0.64`) on each leg.
- Per-slot tints (dominant crafting ore; readable + metallic): helmet sapphire-blue,
  face_mask ruby-red, neck_protection/chestplate/leggings gold shades, boots
  steel-blue. Keep them in a small `ARMOR_TINT` map in this file.
- `applyPalette` is unchanged (it only recolors `paletteMaterials`); armor keeps its
  tint when the skin changes.

### 2. `lib/game/render/playerVisuals.ts` — toggle by what's worn

- Add `equippedArmor: EquippedArmor` to `PlayerVisualsState` (import the type). No
  plumbing needed: `GameRenderer.sync` already passes the full `GameState` (which has
  `equippedArmor`) into `playerVisuals.sync`.
- In `sync`, inside the `visible` branch (after the pose is applied), toggle shells:
  ```ts
  for (const slot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {
    const worn = state.equippedArmor[slot] != null;
    for (const mesh of model.armor[slot]) mesh.visible = worn;
  }
  ```
  Import `ARMOR_SLOTS` from `@/lib/game/items`. (`!= null` works for the v12 instance
  model and is forward/back-compatible.)
- Disposal already covered — armor geometries/materials ride the existing
  `materials`/`geometries` arrays disposed in `playerVisuals.dispose()`.

## Tests (`lib/game/render/playerModel.test.ts`, `playerVisuals.test.ts`)

- `playerModel.test.ts` — `createPlayerModel()` exposes `armor` shells for every
  `ARMOR_SLOT`, all start `visible === false`, and their geometries/materials are
  tracked in `model.geometries`/`model.materials` (so disposal covers them).
- `playerVisuals.test.ts` — `sync` with a third-person camera and a worn piece
  (`equippedArmor.helmet = createSlot("helmet", 1)`) makes that slot's shells
  `visible`, and an empty slot hides them; nothing throws when all slots are empty.
  (Follow the existing render-test setup in these files — a `THREE.Scene` + a fake
  state object.)

## Docs

- `docs/manual.md` / `docs/reference.md` — note that equipped armor is now **shown on
  the player in third-person**.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — add an "Added" bullet under `[Unreleased]` (this rides PR #36, so
  it sits alongside the v12 storage entry).

## Verification

1. `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run format:check && bun test && bun run build`.
2. **Manual pass is the real check** (geometry placement isn't headless-verifiable):
   `bun run dev`, equip each armor piece, press **V** to cycle to third-person
   (rear + front), and confirm each shell sits correctly over its body part, tints by
   its ore, animates with the walk/attack gait, and disappears when unequipped. Switch
   skins to confirm armor keeps its tint over the new body colors. First-person and
   Spectator still hide the body.

## Branch & commits

Commit onto the existing **`fix/armor-dedicated-slots`** branch (PR #36), then push to
update the PR. One focused commit:

- `feat(render): show equipped armor on the third-person player model` — playerModel
  shells + playerVisuals toggle + tests + manual/reference/CHANGELOG.

The branch already carries the unpushed v12 work + the CodeRabbit review fix
(`8dc9fea`); pushing sends all of it. Update the PR title/body to note it now also
adds the body visuals. (Push is user-authorized; do it after the gate is green.)

## Critical files

- `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts` — build armor shells + `armor` map + tints
- `lib/game/render/playerVisuals.ts` — `PlayerVisualsState.equippedArmor` + sync toggle
- `lib/game/render/playerModel.test.ts` / `playerVisuals.test.ts` — coverage
- `docs/manual.md`, `docs/reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Fixed
8	
9	- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
10	
11	### Added
12	
13	- **Grindstone**: a new crafted station (**2 cobble + 2 planks**) — the anvil's inverse, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted stone-wheel block, reusing existing synth) and **no save-format or worldgen change**. Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change
14	- **Anvil**: a new crafted station (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**) for maintaining and consolidating gear, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted dark-iron block, reusing existing synth for its clang). The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
15	  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels. Three actions: **Combine** a duplicate (adds the two durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate); **Repair** with the item's tier material (e.g. diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble for a stone pickaxe) for a chunk of durability without a second copy; and **Rename** (the custom name shows everywhere the item's label does)
16	  - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. The anvil station id is threaded through the **engine/UI** `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`); the panel is a new `AnvilColumn`. A per-item `customName` (additive v11 field, durable gear only, trimmed + capped) persists the rename, surfaced everywhere via a shared `displayName` helper
```

Done — the armor-on-body visuals are implemented, committed, and pushed to **PR #36**.

## What I built
You were right that no armor showed on the body, and I confirmed it was **never implemented** (not a regression). Now:
- **`playerModel.ts`** builds a procedural voxel "shell" per armor piece over the matching body part — helmet→head crown, face mask→front visor, neck protection→collar, chestplate→torso + a shoulder cap on each arm, leggings→upper legs, boots→feet — each parented to the limb pivot so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Shells start hidden.
- **`playerVisuals.ts`** reads `equippedArmor` (already flowing in via `GameRenderer.sync`) and shows the shells for worn slots each frame.
- Renderer-only — no engine/save/logic change.

## Verification
- lint / typecheck / format / build ✓
- `bun test` — **832 pass / 0 fail** (new tests: shells exist + hidden by default; `sync` toggles them by what's worn)
- `bun run test:e2e` — **17 passed**

  "old_string": "  test(\"shows a worn armor piece's shells and hides the rest\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const visuals = createPlayerVisuals(scene);\n    const armor = (slot: \"helmet\" | \"chestplate\") => bodyGroup(scene).getObjectByName(`armor-${slot}`);\n\n    // Nothing worn → all armor shells hidden (sample helmet + chestplate torso).\n    visuals.sync(makeState(), 0);\n    expect(armor(\"helmet\")!.visible).toBe(false);\n    expect(armor(\"chestplate\")!.visible).toBe(false);\n\n    // Wearing a helmet shows its shell, leaves the chestplate hidden.\n    visuals.sync(makeState({ equippedArmor: { ...createEmptyArmorEquipment(), helmet: createSlot(\"helmet\", 1) } }), 16);\n    expect(armor(\"helmet\")!.visible).toBe(true);\n    expect(armor(\"chestplate\")!.visible).toBe(false);\n\n    // Unequipping hides it again.\n    visuals.sync(makeState(), 32);\n    expect(armor(\"helmet\")!.visible).toBe(false);\n    visuals.dispose();",
  "new_string": "  test(\"shows every shell of a worn armor piece and hides the rest\", () => {\n    const scene = new THREE.Scene();\n    const visuals = createPlayerVisuals(scene);\n    // Collect ALL shells for a slot — multi-part slots (chestplate = torso + 2 shoulders)\n    // must toggle together, so a single-mesh check could miss a shell drifting out of sync.\n    const meshesFor = (slot: string) => {\n      const out: THREE.Mesh[] = [];\n      bodyGroup(scene).traverse((obj) => {\n        if (obj instanceof THREE.Mesh && obj.name === `armor-${slot}`) out.push(obj);\n      });\n      return out;\n    };\n    const allHidden = (slot: string) => meshesFor(slot).every((m) => !m.visible);\n    const allShown = (slot: string) => meshesFor(slot).length > 0 && meshesFor(slot).every((m) => m.visible);\n\n    // Nothing worn → all armor shells hidden.\n    visuals.sync(makeState(), 0);\n    expect(allHidden(\"helmet\")).toBe(true);\n    expect(allHidden(\"chestplate\")).toBe(true);\n\n    // Wearing the (multi-part) chestplate shows every one of its shells, helmet stays hidden.\n    visuals.sync(makeState({ equippedArmor: { ...createEmptyArmorEquipment(), chestplate: createSlot(\"chestplate\", 1) } }), 16);\n    expect(meshesFor(\"chestplate\").length).toBeGreaterThan(1);\n    expect(allShown(\"chestplate\")).toBe(true);\n    expect(allHidden(\"helmet\")).toBe(true);\n\n    // Unequipping hides them again.\n    visuals.sync(makeState(), 32);\n    expect(allHidden(\"chestplate\")).toBe(true);\n    visuals.dispose();"
